title: 3ヶ月から3年：今世代のミニゲーム開発者たちは、「長期的な」収益を得始めている
text:
2026年の国慶節の連休中、2026 CICF×AGF広州アニメ・ゲームフェスティバルにおいて、WeChatミニゲームのブースに『跳一跳』の体験コーナーが登場した。
2017年12月28日にリリースされたこのミニゲームは、すでに9年近く存在している。ブースで実施されたアンケートにおいて、「最も印象に残っているミニゲーム」という項目では、依然として『跳一跳』が繰り返し挙げられていた。ブースのスタッフは、ある大学2年生の学生に出会ったが、この国民的ゲームがブームだった当時、彼はまだ小学生だった。
「カジュアルゲームは3ヶ月しか遊べない」という認識は変わりつつあり、同様の事例も増えてきている。『羊了个羊』は爆発的な人気を博した後、一時的に勢いを落としたものの、現在は各種ランキングでトップ3に定着している。『猪了个猪』はリリースから3年近くが経過しているが、サードパーティのデータランキングによると、月間アクティブユーザー数は依然として1000万規模を維持している。データによると、「1億人以上がプレイした」とされる『躺平发育』は、リリースから4年目になっても月間アクティブユーザー数が53.8％のペースで増加しており、ユーザー基盤は常に堅調だ。
01
相場が変化した
WeChatミニゲームのユーザー構成に変化が見られる。
2026年5月に開催されたWeChatミニゲーム開発者カンファレンスで明らかにされたところによると、同プラットフォームの月間アクティブユーザー数は5億人を超え、開発者の数は50万人を超えている。過去1年間で、1日あたりのアクティブユーザー数が100万人を超えるミニゲームは80タイトル以上、四半期ごとの売上高が1000万元を超えるミニゲームは300タイトル以上に上った。WeChatミニゲームのプロダクトディレクターである李卿氏は、会議後のインタビューで、プラットフォーム全体の1日あたりのアクティブユーザー数が1億人を突破したと述べた。開発者の構成では、80％以上が30人未満の中小チームである。大会は「つながりから持続的な成長へ」をテーマに掲げ、製品のイテレーションと長期的な運営を通じて、ミニゲームの持続的な成長を図ることを強調した。
ユーザー層の変化はさらに顕著であり、現在、ミニゲームのプレイヤーは、単に中高年層がカードゲームを楽しむだけにとどまらず、女性ユーザーはパズルゲームやシミュレーションゲームを楽しみ、男性ユーザーはロールプレイングゲームや戦略ゲームを楽しんでおり、ユーザー層全体として明らかに若年化が進んでいる。2026年5月のWeChatミニゲーム開発者カンファレンスで公表されたデータによると、ミニゲームユーザーの53％が男性、47％が女性であり、男女比は比較的均衡している。
外部データとプラットフォームの統計が互いに裏付け合っており、中国音数協ゲーム工作委員会とガンマデータが共同で発表した『2025年中国ゲーム産業報告』によると、2025年の国内ミニプログラムゲーム市場の売上高は535.35億元で、前年比34.39％増となり、そのうちアプリ内課金の売上高は364.64億元、広告収益は170.71億元であった。
2025年のデータ：ミニゲーム市場の規模と成長率（ガンマデータ）
ライフサイクルは、今回の変化において最も重要な指標である。
カジュアルゲームの黎明期、業界では「初日での元本回収」が追求されていましたが、その後7日、30日へと移行し、現在ではカジュアルゲームの回収期間は半年、さらには1年以上にも及ぶようになっています。回収期間の長期化は、開発者が製品のライフサイクルに対して自信を持てるようになったことを意味すると同時に、ユーザーのゲームへの定着度も高まっていることを示しています。
02
ある製品の3年間
『猪了个猪』は、「長青」という方法論を観察するための完全な事例である。このカジュアルパズルミニゲームは同趣科技によって開発され、2023年にリリースされて以来、2026年に至るまで、ミニゲーム人気ランキングの上位をキープし続けている。
同趣科技の創業者であるウィリアム氏によると、同社のチームは約200人で構成され、「中台」と小規模プロジェクトを組み合わせた組織体制を採用しており、これまでに累計で100以上の製品を開発してきたという。
『猪了个猪』の立ち上げは、外部の予想とは裏腹に、サービス開始当初の広告ROIは予想の6～7割にとどまった。チームは広告運用からゲーム本体のステージ調整へと重点を移し、まずユーザー行動データを継続的に分析し、プレイヤーがどのステージで詰まっているか、どのポイントで離脱しているか、広告表示に対する反応はどうなのかを観察した。その後、複数回のABテストを重ね、1人あたりの平均プレイ時間や広告浸透率などの指標が理想的な範囲に収まるまで調整を行い、ようやく広告出稿量を段階的に増やしていった。この過程でチームは豊富なステージ調整の経験を蓄積し、その後の継続的な最適化、コンテンツの反復改善、そして異なるタイプのプレイヤーに合わせた差別化された設計を行うための基盤を築いた。
難易度曲線は、この種の製品において最も重要な要素であり、ウィリアムはこれについて詳しく説明しました。初心者段階では難易度を低く設定し、プレイヤーに自信を持たせ、中盤では段階的に難易度を引き上げ、急激な難易度の上昇を避ける必要があります。プレイヤーがステージで詰まってしまった際、インセンティブ動画広告は「助けを求める」ための選択肢として設計されており、プレイヤーは広告を視聴してヒントを得たり、操作をやり直したり、あるいは直接再挑戦したりすることができ、選択権はユーザー自身にあります。
チームは各ステージの再挑戦回数や離脱データを監視しており、特定のステージの再挑戦率が高すぎれば難易度を下げ、数ステージ連続で挑戦した後には、プレイヤーが息抜きできるようボーナスステージを用意しています。ウィリアムの言葉を借りれば、「勝ち続けるとプレイヤーは飽きてしまうし、負け続けるとプレイヤーは離れてしまう。「優れた難易度曲線とは、プレイヤーに『あと少しでクリアできる』と感じさせ、もう一度挑戦したくなるようなものです。」
シンプルで、楽しくて、やみつきになる
ユーザー獲得の面では、広告購入が依然として基盤となっているが、クリエイティブのハードルはショート動画のフィードによって再定義されている。ウィリアム氏は、ユーザーが広告素材を目にしてから3秒以内に遊び方が理解できない場合、コンバージョン率は必然的に低くなり、こうした参入障壁の高い製品は、ミニゲームの最も重要な拡散基盤を直接失うことになると指摘している。
ユーザー定着の段階では、既存ユーザーの呼び戻しを厳格に層別化し、高価値ユーザーのみに予算を投入する。浅い関与の一時的なプレイヤーの呼び戻しはコストが高く、コンバージョン率も低いため、通常は見送る。再活性化施策も控えめに実施し、バージョンの大規模アップデートや大型ステージパックの追加時のみ、プラットフォームの規定に沿ったチャネルを通じてアプローチを行い、復帰特典と組み合わせることで、再プレイのハードルを下げる。同時に、復帰ユーザーの過去のアクティブ利用状況に基づいてさらにきめ細かなセグメンテーションを行い、各層のユーザーに合わせて難易度やペースを調整した設計を施すことで、復帰ユーザーのゲーム体験を継続的に最適化し、長期的な定着率の向上を図ります。
広告とユーザー体験のバランスは、チームにとって生命線と見なされている。ウィリアム氏によると、社内には厳格なルールがあり、広告の掲載位置や表示頻度の変更を行う際は、必ずARPUと継続利用率を同時に監視しなければならない。継続利用率が著しく低下した場合は直ちに元に戻し、短期的な収益向上のみを目的とした変更は一切却下されるという。
「ユーザー定着率はIAA製品の基盤であり、広告収益化はその結果に過ぎない。本末転倒であってはならない」と彼は指摘する。一部の製品では、広告収入を伸ばすために広告枠を詰め込み、短期的には収入が増加するものの、ユーザー定着率が低下した結果、全体としてのLTVが逆に低下してしまう。多くのチームがこの全体的な収支計算を誤っているのだ。
03
どのようなミニゲームが「不朽の名作」と言えるのでしょうか？
いったいどのような製品が「ロングセラー」と言えるのだろうか。業界やメーカーの視点から見ると、その答えは多少異なるかもしれない。
期間の面から見ると、ミニゲームが2～3年以上運営され、スマホゲームのライフサイクルに匹敵するものであってこそ、ロングセラーゲームと呼べる。もちろん、個々のタイトルの潜在力を判断するには、ユーザー規模、ユーザープロファイル、経営指標など、多角的な視点から検討する必要があり、具体的な事例については個別に分析する必要がある。
注目すべきは、ゲームプレイには周期性があり、長期的に人気を博す製品には共通点が見られるという点だ。すなわち、定番のゲームプレイに微細な革新が加わっているということである。『羊了个羊』や『猪了个猪』、あるいは2026年に大ヒットした『趙雲と阿斗』といったゲームは、いずれも定番のゲームプレイを基盤としつつ、新たなメカニズムやテーマを盛り込むことで、「古いゲームプレイ」に新たな活力を吹き込んでいる。歴史の彼方に埋もれたゲームプレイは、現段階では人気がないとしても、依然として再生のチャンスを秘めている。
2026年上半期のWeChatミニゲーム広告展開の動向
ウィリアムの判断基準はデータシグナルに重きを置いている。彼は、チームが注目しているのは成長ロジックの転換であり、ユーザー獲得による新規ユーザー数の拡大が鈍化し、収益構造が既存ユーザーの再利用へと移行していることは、製品が次の段階に入ったことを意味すると述べた。もし新規ユーザーの長期的な定着率が低下し続けるならば、たとえ日次アクティブユーザー数が依然として高い水準にあっても、製品は実質的に衰退期に入っていることになる。
失敗した製品について、同趣は4つの共通点を洗い出した。それは、「ゲームプレイが3秒以内に理解できない」「コアループに即時フィードバックが欠けている」「他社製品と似通った『スキンを変えただけ』の製品で印象に残らない」「ゲームプレイをショート動画で表現できない」という点である。製品の廃止基準も同様に明確であり、中核となるループがデータによって否定された、収益化モデルが長期的に成立しない、改善の余地が枯渇した――この3つがすべて揃って初めて投資を停止し、その後、サーバーを維持しつつ段階的に配信を停止するメンテナンス期間に入る。William氏は「検証可能な仮説が残っている段階で即座に打ち切ることはなく、製品を終了するたびに、チームは振り返りを行う必要がある」と付け加えた。
この業界には、ひっそりと走り続けるランナーたちもいる。
例えば『躺平发育』がその一つだ。このゲームは2022年初頭にリリースされ、『羊了个羊』よりもさらに早く登場した。アイデアが爆発的な人気を博して以来、そのライフサイクルは現在まで続いており、ユーザーは学生が中心だ。開発チームのスタイルは控えめで、メディアとの接触はほとんどなく、まさに「隠れた大ボス」と呼ぶにふさわしい存在である。
04
政策のバランス
プラットフォームのポリシーと能力は、長青ゲームの成長を支えるもう一つの環境を形成している。
2026年8月、当プラットフォームはIAAインセンティブプログラムの新たなアップグレードを実施しました。広告を主な収益源とするゲームにおいて、テンセント広告および外部アプリによるユーザー獲得を通じて登録または再訪問したユーザーについて、アクティブ時間の基準要件が「当日、ゲーム内で5分以上アクティブである」から「登録以来の累計アクティブ時間が3分以上である」へと緩和されました。
プラットフォーム側は、1日あたりの利用時間を「累計利用時間」に変更したことで、ユーザーの実際の利用パターンにより即した形となり、より多くの有効ユーザーがインセンティブの対象となるようになると説明した。
長期インセンティブの期間が延長され、従来の「1日目から90日目の広告売上高の35％」が、「1日目から180日目の広告売上高の35％」に調整されました。開発者は、「1日目から30日目の広告売上高の40％」という軽・中程度のプランと長期プランの中から自由に選択できます。ライフサイクルが長く、ユーザーの継続的なアクティブ率が高い製品ほど、より充実したインセンティブ支援を受けることができます。
さらに、45日以上離脱していたユーザーが、要件を満たすユーザー獲得シナリオを通じて復帰し、累積アクティブ利用時間に達した場合、登録ユーザーと同等のインセンティブ特典を受けることができます。利用時間の要件を引き下げ、インセンティブ期間を延長することで、開発者が質の高いアプリを磨き上げ、長期的なユーザー定着を着実に図り、より安定した収益を得られるよう支援することを目的としています。
一方で、新しいツールやコンテンツ形式によって、長期的な取り組みのハードルが下がりつつあります。当プラットフォームでは今年、収益診断・最適化ツールをリリースしました。このツールは、開発者がコアユーザー、準コアユーザー、一般ユーザーの広告獲得分布を区別できるよう支援するとともに、業界のベンチマークデータを参照用として提供することで、チームが問題が製品そのものにあるのか、それとも広告配信戦略にあるのかを判断できるようにします。
ミニゲームの収益診断・最適化ツール
コンテンツ面では、『永夜起源』などの作品が、AI漫画ドラマとミニゲームの組み合わせを試み始めている。漫画ドラマがキャラクターの塑造や視聴者の獲得を担い、ゲームがその流れを引き継いでコンバージョンを促進するという、かつては大企業にしか実現できなかったこのコンテンツ戦略が、現在、中小規模のチームにも広がりつつある。
もちろん、WeChatでのシェアは依然としてWeChatミニゲームにとって長期的に有効なユーザー獲得手段であり、現在、開発者たちは「シェアの入口を設ける」ことから「シェア体験をデザインする」ことへと段階的に移行しつつあり、プレイヤーがシェアしたいと思った瞬間に、シェアする価値のあるコンテンツを提供できるようにしています。さらに、プラットフォームではPKチャレンジや「青い封筒」によるギフト贈呈といった新しいソーシャル機能も導入され、よりインタラクティブな設計によってシェアの効率を高めています。
最近、『憧れの生活』は「プラットフォームのソーシャルレッドパケット＋シェア」を活用し、シェアしたユーザーと友人の双方が現金レッドパケットを受け取れる仕組みを導入しました。これにより、シェアによる報酬が実際の交流に結びつき、招待されたユーザーの有料化率や新規ユーザーの初回継続率が、従来のユーザー獲得手法に比べて向上し、ユーザーの質も高まり、ROIの効率が著しく向上しました。
長青の設立後、次の難関がすでに浮上している。
『羊了个羊』と『抓大鹅』は、ミニゲームのIP化における模範例であり、両タイトルともグッズを発売し、オフラインのコミックイベントに参加したほか、京東（JD.com）とのコラボレーションも行ったことがある。ウィリアム氏によると、同趣はすでに『猪了个猪』のぬいぐるみグッズを販売しており、ゲームキャラクターとアニメドラマの融合も試みている。同氏は、テンセントのエコシステムがIPの拡大においてさらなる支援を提供してくれることを期待している。
「長青」が、ごく一部の製品に恵まれた幸運から、議論・検証・再現が可能な道筋へと変化したとき、いかにして真のIPやブランド価値を育むか――これこそが、ミニゲームが新たな段階において避けては通れない課題となるだろう。

2017年12月28日にリリースされたこのミニゲームは、すでに9年近く存在している。ブースで実施されたアンケートにおいて、「最も印象に残っているミニゲーム」という項目では、依然として『跳一跳』が繰り返し挙げられていた。ブースのスタッフは、ある大学2年生の学生に出会ったが、この国民的ゲームがブームだった当時、彼はまだ小学生だった。

『猪了个猪』の立ち上げは、外部の予想とは裏腹に、サービス開始当初の広告ROIは予想の6～7割にとどまった。チームは広告運用からゲーム本体のステージ調整へと重点を移し、まずユーザー行動データを継続的に分析し、プレイヤーがどのステージで詰まっているか、どのポイントで離脱しているか、広告表示に対する反応はどうなのかを観察した。その後、複数回のABテストを重ね、1人あたりの平均プレイ時間や広告浸透率などの指標が理想的な範囲に収まるまで調整を行い、ようやく広告出稿量を段階的に増やしていった。この過程でチームは豊富なステージ調整の経験を蓄積し、その後の継続的な最適化、コンテンツの反復改善、そして異なるタイプのプレイヤーに合わせた差別化された設計を行うための基盤を築いた。

難易度曲線は、この種の製品において最も重要な要素であり、ウィリアムはこれについて詳しく説明しました。初心者段階では難易度を低く設定し、プレイヤーに自信を持たせ、中盤では段階的に難易度を引き上げ、急激な難易度の上昇を避ける必要があります。プレイヤーがステージで詰まってしまった際、インセンティブ動画広告は「助けを求める」ための選択肢として設計されており、プレイヤーは広告を視聴してヒントを得たり、操作をやり直したり、あるいは直接再挑戦したりすることができ、選択権はユーザー自身にあります。

チームは各ステージの再挑戦回数や離脱データを監視しており、特定のステージの再挑戦率が高すぎれば難易度を下げ、数ステージ連続で挑戦した後には、プレイヤーが息抜きできるようボーナスステージを用意しています。ウィリアムの言葉を借りれば、「勝ち続けるとプレイヤーは飽きてしまうし、負け続けるとプレイヤーは離れてしまう。「優れた難易度曲線とは、プレイヤーに『あと少しでクリアできる』と感じさせ、もう一度挑戦したくなるようなものです。」

シンプルで、楽しくて、やみつきになる

ユーザー獲得の面では、広告購入が依然として基盤となっているが、クリエイティブのハードルはショート動画のフィードによって再定義されている。ウィリアム氏は、ユーザーが広告素材を目にしてから3秒以内に遊び方が理解できない場合、コンバージョン率は必然的に低くなり、こうした参入障壁の高い製品は、ミニゲームの最も重要な拡散基盤を直接失うことになると指摘している。

ユーザー定着の段階では、既存ユーザーの呼び戻しを厳格に層別化し、高価値ユーザーのみに予算を投入する。浅い関与の一時的なプレイヤーの呼び戻しはコストが高く、コンバージョン率も低いため、通常は見送る。再活性化施策も控えめに実施し、バージョンの大規模アップデートや大型ステージパックの追加時のみ、プラットフォームの規定に沿ったチャネルを通じてアプローチを行い、復帰特典と組み合わせることで、再プレイのハードルを下げる。同時に、復帰ユーザーの過去のアクティブ利用状況に基づいてさらにきめ細かなセグメンテーションを行い、各層のユーザーに合わせて難易度やペースを調整した設計を施すことで、復帰ユーザーのゲーム体験を継続的に最適化し、長期的な定着率の向上を図ります。

広告とユーザー体験のバランスは、チームにとって生命線と見なされている。ウィリアム氏によると、社内には厳格なルールがあり、広告の掲載位置や表示頻度の変更を行う際は、必ずARPUと継続利用率を同時に監視しなければならない。継続利用率が著しく低下した場合は直ちに元に戻し、短期的な収益向上のみを目的とした変更は一切却下されるという。

「ユーザー定着率はIAA製品の基盤であり、広告収益化はその結果に過ぎない。本末転倒であってはならない」と彼は指摘する。一部の製品では、広告収入を伸ばすために広告枠を詰め込み、短期的には収入が増加するものの、ユーザー定着率が低下した結果、全体としてのLTVが逆に低下してしまう。多くのチームがこの全体的な収支計算を誤っているのだ。

03

どのようなミニゲームが「不朽の名作」と言えるのでしょうか？

いったいどのような製品が「ロングセラー」と言えるのだろうか。業界やメーカーの視点から見ると、その答えは多少異なるかもしれない。

期間の面から見ると、ミニゲームが2～3年以上運営され、スマホゲームのライフサイクルに匹敵するものであってこそ、ロングセラーゲームと呼べる。もちろん、個々のタイトルの潜在力を判断するには、ユーザー規模、ユーザープロファイル、経営指標など、多角的な視点から検討する必要があり、具体的な事例については個別に分析する必要がある。

注目すべきは、ゲームプレイには周期性があり、長期的に人気を博す製品には共通点が見られるという点だ。すなわち、定番のゲームプレイに微細な革新が加わっているということである。『羊了个羊』や『猪了个猪』、あるいは2026年に大ヒットした『趙雲と阿斗』といったゲームは、いずれも定番のゲームプレイを基盤としつつ、新たなメカニズムやテーマを盛り込むことで、「古いゲームプレイ」に新たな活力を吹き込んでいる。歴史の彼方に埋もれたゲームプレイは、現段階では人気がないとしても、依然として再生のチャンスを秘めている。

2026年上半期のWeChatミニゲーム広告展開の動向

ウィリアムの判断基準はデータシグナルに重きを置いている。彼は、チームが注目しているのは成長ロジックの転換であり、ユーザー獲得による新規ユーザー数の拡大が鈍化し、収益構造が既存ユーザーの再利用へと移行していることは、製品が次の段階に入ったことを意味すると述べた。もし新規ユーザーの長期的な定着率が低下し続けるならば、たとえ日次アクティブユーザー数が依然として高い水準にあっても、製品は実質的に衰退期に入っていることになる。

失敗した製品について、同趣は4つの共通点を洗い出した。それは、「ゲームプレイが3秒以内に理解できない」「コアループに即時フィードバックが欠けている」「他社製品と似通った『スキンを変えただけ』の製品で印象に残らない」「ゲームプレイをショート動画で表現できない」という点である。製品の廃止基準も同様に明確であり、中核となるループがデータによって否定された、収益化モデルが長期的に成立しない、改善の余地が枯渇した――この3つがすべて揃って初めて投資を停止し、その後、サーバーを維持しつつ段階的に配信を停止するメンテナンス期間に入る。William氏は「検証可能な仮説が残っている段階で即座に打ち切ることはなく、製品を終了するたびに、チームは振り返りを行う必要がある」と付け加えた。

この業界には、ひっそりと走り続けるランナーたちもいる。

例えば『躺平发育』がその一つだ。このゲームは2022年初頭にリリースされ、『羊了个羊』よりもさらに早く登場した。アイデアが爆発的な人気を博して以来、そのライフサイクルは現在まで続いており、ユーザーは学生が中心だ。開発チームのスタイルは控えめで、メディアとの接触はほとんどなく、まさに「隠れた大ボス」と呼ぶにふさわしい存在である。

04

政策のバランス

プラットフォームのポリシーと能力は、長青ゲームの成長を支えるもう一つの環境を形成している。

2026年8月、当プラットフォームはIAAインセンティブプログラムの新たなアップグレードを実施しました。広告を主な収益源とするゲームにおいて、テンセント広告および外部アプリによるユーザー獲得を通じて登録または再訪問したユーザーについて、アクティブ時間の基準要件が「当日、ゲーム内で5分以上アクティブである」から「登録以来の累計アクティブ時間が3分以上である」へと緩和されました。

プラットフォーム側は、1日あたりの利用時間を「累計利用時間」に変更したことで、ユーザーの実際の利用パターンにより即した形となり、より多くの有効ユーザーがインセンティブの対象となるようになると説明した。

長期インセンティブの期間が延長され、従来の「1日目から90日目の広告売上高の35％」が、「1日目から180日目の広告売上高の35％」に調整されました。開発者は、「1日目から30日目の広告売上高の40％」という軽・中程度のプランと長期プランの中から自由に選択できます。ライフサイクルが長く、ユーザーの継続的なアクティブ率が高い製品ほど、より充実したインセンティブ支援を受けることができます。

さらに、45日以上離脱していたユーザーが、要件を満たすユーザー獲得シナリオを通じて復帰し、累積アクティブ利用時間に達した場合、登録ユーザーと同等のインセンティブ特典を受けることができます。利用時間の要件を引き下げ、インセンティブ期間を延長することで、開発者が質の高いアプリを磨き上げ、長期的なユーザー定着を着実に図り、より安定した収益を得られるよう支援することを目的としています。

一方で、新しいツールやコンテンツ形式によって、長期的な取り組みのハードルが下がりつつあります。当プラットフォームでは今年、収益診断・最適化ツールをリリースしました。このツールは、開発者がコアユーザー、準コアユーザー、一般ユーザーの広告獲得分布を区別できるよう支援するとともに、業界のベンチマークデータを参照用として提供することで、チームが問題が製品そのものにあるのか、それとも広告配信戦略にあるのかを判断できるようにします。

ミニゲームの収益診断・最適化ツール

コンテンツ面では、『永夜起源』などの作品が、AI漫画ドラマとミニゲームの組み合わせを試み始めている。漫画ドラマがキャラクターの塑造や視聴者の獲得を担い、ゲームがその流れを引き継いでコンバージョンを促進するという、かつては大企業にしか実現できなかったこのコンテンツ戦略が、現在、中小規模のチームにも広がりつつある。

もちろん、WeChatでのシェアは依然としてWeChatミニゲームにとって長期的に有効なユーザー獲得手段であり、現在、開発者たちは「シェアの入口を設ける」ことから「シェア体験をデザインする」ことへと段階的に移行しつつあり、プレイヤーがシェアしたいと思った瞬間に、シェアする価値のあるコンテンツを提供できるようにしています。さらに、プラットフォームではPKチャレンジや「青い封筒」によるギフト贈呈といった新しいソーシャル機能も導入され、よりインタラクティブな設計によってシェアの効率を高めています。

最近、『憧れの生活』は「プラットフォームのソーシャルレッドパケット＋シェア」を活用し、シェアしたユーザーと友人の双方が現金レッドパケットを受け取れる仕組みを導入しました。これにより、シェアによる報酬が実際の交流に結びつき、招待されたユーザーの有料化率や新規ユーザーの初回継続率が、従来のユーザー獲得手法に比べて向上し、ユーザーの質も高まり、ROIの効率が著しく向上しました。

長青の設立後、次の難関がすでに浮上している。

『羊了个羊』と『抓大鹅』は、ミニゲームのIP化における模範例であり、両タイトルともグッズを発売し、オフラインのコミックイベントに参加したほか、京東（JD.com）とのコラボレーションも行ったことがある。ウィリアム氏によると、同趣はすでに『猪了个猪』のぬいぐるみグッズを販売しており、ゲームキャラクターとアニメドラマの融合も試みている。同氏は、テンセントのエコシステムがIPの拡大においてさらなる支援を提供してくれることを期待している。

「長青」が、ごく一部の製品に恵まれた幸運から、議論・検証・再現が可能な道筋へと変化したとき、いかにして真のIPやブランド価値を育むか――これこそが、ミニゲームが新たな段階において避けては通れない課題となるだろう。

title: From Three Months to Three Years: This Generation of Mini-Game Developers Is Starting to Make Money in the “Long Run”
text:
During the 2026 National Day holiday, at the 2026 CICF×AGF Guangzhou Animation and Gaming Festival, a demo booth for *Jump Jump* was set up at the WeChat Mini Games exhibit.
This mini-game, which launched on December 28, 2017, has been around for nearly nine years. In the booth survey, under the category “Most Memorable Mini-Game,” *Jump Jump* continues to be mentioned time and again. Staff at the booth met a sophomore college student who was still in elementary school when this nationwide sensation first took the country by storm.
The perception that casual games can only be played for three months is changing, and similar stories are becoming more common. *Sheep Sheep* experienced a massive surge followed by a decline,and has now stabilized in the top three on various charts. *Piggy Pig* has been live for nearly three years, and third-party data shows its monthly active users remain in the tens of millions. Data indicates that *Lie Flat and Level Up*—which “over 100 million people have played”—continues to see its monthly active users grow at a rate of 53.8% in its fourth year since launch, with a consistently robust user base.
01
The market has changed.
The user demographics of WeChat Mini Games are changing.
According to information disclosed at the May 2026 WeChat Mini Games Developer Conference, the platform has over 500 million monthly active users and more than 500,000 developers. Over the past year, more than 80 mini games have exceeded 1 million daily active users, and more than 300 mini games have generated quarterly revenue exceeding 10 million yuan.In a post-conference interview, Li Qing, Product Director of WeChat Mini Games, also stated that the platform’s total daily active users have surpassed 100 million. In terms of developer composition, more than 80% are small and medium-sized teams with fewer than 30 members. Under the theme “From Connection to Longevity,” the conference emphasized enabling the sustained growth of mini games through product iteration and long-term operations.
The shift in the user base has been even more pronounced. Today, WeChat Mini Games are no longer limited to middle-aged and older adults playing card and board games; female users can enjoy match-three and simulation games, while male users can find role-playing and strategy games. Overall, the user demographic is clearly becoming younger.According to data disclosed at the WeChat Mini-Games Developer Conference in May 2026, men account for 53% of mini-game users and women account for 47%, representing a relatively balanced gender distribution.
External data corroborates the platform’s figures. According to the “2025 China Game Industry Report” jointly released by the Game Working Committee of the China Audio-Video and Digital Publishing Association and Gamma Data,in 2025, the domestic mini-program game market generated revenue of 53.535 billion yuan, a year-over-year increase of 34.39 percent, with in-app purchases accounting for 36.464 billion yuan and advertising revenue totaling 17.071 billion yuan.
2025 Data: Mini-Game Market Size and Growth Rate (Gamma Data)
Lifecycle is the most critical metric in this round of changes.
In the early days of casual games, the industry aimed to recoup costs on the first day; this later shifted to 7 days and then 30 days. Today, casual games have extended their payback periods to half a year or even longer. This lengthening of the payback period indicates that developers have gained confidence in the product lifecycle, and user retention is also improving.
02
Three Years of a Product
“Piggy Pig” is a prime example of the “Evergreen” methodology. Developed by Tongqu Technology, this casual puzzle game was launched in 2023 and remained at the top of the mini-game popularity charts through 2026.
William, founder of Tongqu Technology, revealed that the company has a team of about 200 people, operates under an organizational structure combining a central platform with small projects, and has developed over a hundred products to date.
Contrary to outside expectations, “Piggy Pig” got off to a slow start; when it first launched, its ad ROI reached only 60 to 70 percent of projections.so the team shifted its focus from advertising to optimizing the game’s levels. They began by continuously analyzing user behavior data—observing which levels players got stuck on, at which points they dropped off, and how they responded to ad triggers—before conducting multiple rounds of A/B testing. Only after metrics such as average playtime per user and ad penetration rate were adjusted to the ideal range did they gradually scale up their operations.Throughout this process, the team accumulated extensive experience in level optimization, laying the foundation for their ongoing optimization, content iteration, and differentiated design tailored to different types of players.
The difficulty curve is the most critical aspect of this type of product, and William provided a detailed explanation: the beginner stage must be simple to help players build confidence, while the difficulty in the mid-game should increase gradually in steps to avoid a sudden, steep rise.When players get stuck, rewarded video ads are designed as an option for active assistance. Players can watch an ad to receive a hint or undo their last move, or they can simply retry—the choice is entirely up to the user.
The team monitors the number of retries and drop-off rates for each level. If the retry rate for a particular level is too high, they lower its difficulty. After several consecutive challenging levels, they also include bonus levels to give players a breather. As William puts it, “You can’t let players win all the time—they’ll get bored—but you can’t let them lose all the time either—they’ll quit.”A good difficulty curve makes players feel like they’re just a hair’s breadth away from passing, so they’re willing to try again.”
Simple, fun, and addictive
On the user acquisition side, paid user acquisition remains the foundation, but the bar for creativity has been redefined by short-video feeds. William noted that if players come across an ad and cannot understand the gameplay within three seconds, the conversion rate will naturally be low; products with such a high learning curve will directly lose the most fundamental basis for the spread of mini-games.
In terms of user retention, efforts to re-engage existing users are strictly segmented by tier; budget is allocated only for high-value users. Re-engaging casual, one-time players is costly and yields low conversion rates, so these efforts are typically abandoned.Reactivation efforts are also kept to a minimum, with outreach conducted only through platform-compliant channels during major version updates or the release of new large-scale level packs, complemented by return rewards to lower the barrier to re-engagement.At the same time, based on the historical activity patterns of returning users, we further refine segmentation and tailor the difficulty and pacing to each segment, continuously optimizing the gaming experience for returning users to enhance their long-term retention.
The team views the balance between advertising and user experience as a lifeline. William revealed that the company has strict internal rules: any changes to ad placements or frequency must be accompanied by simultaneous monitoring of ARPU and retention rates; if retention drops significantly, the changes are immediately reversed, and any changes aimed solely at short-term revenue growth are categorically rejected.
“Retention is the foundation of IAA products, while ad monetization is the result—we must not put the cart before the horse,” he said. He believes that some products increase ad impressions to boost ad revenue; while this leads to a short-term rise in revenue, retention eventually declines, causing overall LTV to drop instead. Many teams have miscalculated this balance.
03
What Makes a Casual Game a “Long-Running Hit”?
What exactly constitutes a timeless product? From the perspectives of the industry and manufacturers, the answer may vary slightly.
In terms of time, a mini-game must be in operation for two to three years or more—a lifespan comparable to that of a mobile game—to be considered an evergreen game. Of course, assessing the potential of a single title requires examining multiple factors, such as user base, user demographics, and operational metrics; each specific case must be analyzed on its own merits.
It’s worth noting that game mechanics follow cyclical patterns, and long-running products share a common trait: classic gameplay combined with subtle innovations.Whether it’s *Sheep Sheep*, *Pig Pig*, or the 2026 hit *Zhao Yun and A Dou*, all of these games build upon classic gameplay by introducing new mechanics or thematic elements, breathing new life into “old” games.Gameplay concepts long forgotten by history, though not currently popular, still have the opportunity to be reborn.
WeChat Mini-Game Advertising Landscape in the First Half of 2026
William’s analysis focuses more on data signals. He explained that the team looks for shifts in growth dynamics: when user acquisition no longer drives significant growth and revenue shifts toward repeat engagement from existing users, it signals that the product has entered its next phase. If new user retention continues to weaken over the long term, even if daily active users remain high, the product has effectively entered a period of decline.
Regarding failed products, Tongqu identified four common characteristics: gameplay that can’t be understood within three seconds; a core loop lacking immediate feedback; homogenized “skin-swap” designs with no memorable features; and gameplay that cannot be demonstrated through short videos.The criteria for discontinuing a product are equally clear: the core loop is disproved by data, the monetization model remains unsustainable over the long term, and there is no room for further iteration. Only when all three conditions are met will investment be halted, after which the product enters a maintenance phase involving server retention and the gradual shutdown of advertising campaigns. William added, “We won’t ax a product outright while there are still testable hypotheses remaining;and every time a product is shut down, the team must conduct a post-mortem.”
There are also some quiet long-distance runners in the industry.
For example, *Lie Flat and Level Up* is one such game. Launched in early 2022—even before *Sheep Sheep*—it has maintained its popularity long after its initial creative surge. With a user base primarily consisting of students and a low-key development team that rarely interacts with the media, it can truly be called a “hidden big boss.”
04
Policy Balance
The platform’s policies and capabilities form the other half of the environment in which Changqing Games thrives.
In August 2026, the platform rolled out a new round of upgrades to the IAA incentive program. For games where advertising is the primary revenue source, the duration requirement for users who registered or returned via Tencent Ads or external user acquisition channels was relaxed from “being active in the game for more than 5 minutes on the same day” to “having been active for a cumulative total of more than 3 minutes since registration.”
The platform explained that changing the metric from daily usage time to cumulative usage over time better reflects users’ actual activity patterns and helps bring more active users into the incentive program.
The duration of the long-term incentive program has been extended accordingly; the original “35% of ad revenue from days 1 to 90” has been adjusted to “35% of ad revenue from days 1 to 180.”Developers may choose between the “40% of ad revenue from days 1 to 30” light-to-moderate plan and the long-term plan. Products with longer lifecycles and stronger user retention capabilities will receive more substantial incentive support.
In addition, users who have been inactive for more than 45 days and return through eligible user acquisition scenarios—after reaching the required cumulative active time—are eligible for the same incentives as registered users. With lower time thresholds and a longer incentive period, the goal is to help developers refine high-quality products, strategically build long-term user retention, and achieve more stable returns.
At the same time, new tools and content formats are lowering the barriers to long-term success. This year, the platform launched a revenue diagnosis and optimization tool to help developers distinguish between the user acquisition distribution of core users, secondary core users, and casual users, and to provide industry benchmark data for comparison—enabling teams to determine whether the problem lies with the product itself or with their advertising strategy.
Mini-Game Revenue Diagnostic and Optimization Tool
On the content side, products such as *Eternal Night: Origins* are beginning to experiment with combining AI-generated animated series with mini-games, where the animated series is responsible for character development and attracting viewers, while the games handle conversion. This content strategy—which in the past only large companies had the resources to implement—is now spreading to small and medium-sized teams.
Of course, sharing via WeChat remains a long-term and effective way for WeChat Mini Games to acquire users. Today, developers are gradually shifting their focus from simply “setting up sharing entry points” to “designing the sharing experience,” ensuring that players are provided with content worth sharing at the exact moment they feel the urge to do so.In addition, the platform has introduced new social features such as head-to-head challenges and blue envelope gifting, using more interactive designs to boost sharing efficiency.
Recently, the show *The Ideal Life* leveraged a “platform social red envelope + sharing” mechanism, where both the sharer and their friends receive cash red envelopes. This approach ensures that sharing rewards drive genuine interaction. Compared to traditional user acquisition methods, the paid user penetration, new user acquisition, and retention rates among invited users are higher, resulting in better user quality and significantly improved ROI.
With Evergreen’s establishment, the next hurdle has already come into view.
“Sheep, Sheep” and “Catch the Goose” are prime examples of mini-games being turned into IPs; both titles have launched merchandise, participated in offline comic conventions, and have collaborated with JD.com.William revealed that Tongqu is already selling plush toys based on *Piggy Pig* and is exploring ways to integrate the game’s characters into animated series. He hopes that the Tencent ecosystem can provide more support in amplifying the IP’s reach.
Once the success of a few products—which was once a matter of luck—evolves into a proven, verifiable, and replicable model, the question of how to cultivate genuine IP and brand value will likely become an unavoidable challenge for mini-games as they enter this new phase.

During the 2026 National Day holiday, at the 2026 CICF×AGF Guangzhou Animation and Gaming Festival, a demo booth for *Jump Jump* was set up at the WeChat Mini Games exhibit.

This mini-game, which launched on December 28, 2017, has been around for nearly nine years. In the booth survey, under the category “Most Memorable Mini-Game,” *Jump Jump* continues to be mentioned time and again. Staff at the booth met a sophomore college student who was still in elementary school when this nationwide sensation first took the country by storm.

The perception that casual games can only be played for three months is changing, and similar stories are becoming more common. *Sheep Sheep* experienced a massive surge followed by a decline,and has now stabilized in the top three on various charts. *Piggy Pig* has been live for nearly three years, and third-party data shows its monthly active users remain in the tens of millions. Data indicates that *Lie Flat and Level Up*—which “over 100 million people have played”—continues to see its monthly active users grow at a rate of 53.8% in its fourth year since launch, with a consistently robust user base.

01

The market has changed.

The user demographics of WeChat Mini Games are changing.

According to information disclosed at the May 2026 WeChat Mini Games Developer Conference, the platform has over 500 million monthly active users and more than 500,000 developers. Over the past year, more than 80 mini games have exceeded 1 million daily active users, and more than 300 mini games have generated quarterly revenue exceeding 10 million yuan.In a post-conference interview, Li Qing, Product Director of WeChat Mini Games, also stated that the platform’s total daily active users have surpassed 100 million. In terms of developer composition, more than 80% are small and medium-sized teams with fewer than 30 members. Under the theme “From Connection to Longevity,” the conference emphasized enabling the sustained growth of mini games through product iteration and long-term operations.

The shift in the user base has been even more pronounced. Today, WeChat Mini Games are no longer limited to middle-aged and older adults playing card and board games; female users can enjoy match-three and simulation games, while male users can find role-playing and strategy games. Overall, the user demographic is clearly becoming younger.According to data disclosed at the WeChat Mini-Games Developer Conference in May 2026, men account for 53% of mini-game users and women account for 47%, representing a relatively balanced gender distribution.

External data corroborates the platform’s figures. According to the “2025 China Game Industry Report” jointly released by the Game Working Committee of the China Audio-Video and Digital Publishing Association and Gamma Data,in 2025, the domestic mini-program game market generated revenue of 53.535 billion yuan, a year-over-year increase of 34.39 percent, with in-app purchases accounting for 36.464 billion yuan and advertising revenue totaling 17.071 billion yuan.

2025 Data: Mini-Game Market Size and Growth Rate (Gamma Data)

Lifecycle is the most critical metric in this round of changes.

In the early days of casual games, the industry aimed to recoup costs on the first day; this later shifted to 7 days and then 30 days. Today, casual games have extended their payback periods to half a year or even longer. This lengthening of the payback period indicates that developers have gained confidence in the product lifecycle, and user retention is also improving.

02

Three Years of a Product

“Piggy Pig” is a prime example of the “Evergreen” methodology. Developed by Tongqu Technology, this casual puzzle game was launched in 2023 and remained at the top of the mini-game popularity charts through 2026.

William, founder of Tongqu Technology, revealed that the company has a team of about 200 people, operates under an organizational structure combining a central platform with small projects, and has developed over a hundred products to date.

Contrary to outside expectations, “Piggy Pig” got off to a slow start; when it first launched, its ad ROI reached only 60 to 70 percent of projections.so the team shifted its focus from advertising to optimizing the game’s levels. They began by continuously analyzing user behavior data—observing which levels players got stuck on, at which points they dropped off, and how they responded to ad triggers—before conducting multiple rounds of A/B testing. Only after metrics such as average playtime per user and ad penetration rate were adjusted to the ideal range did they gradually scale up their operations.Throughout this process, the team accumulated extensive experience in level optimization, laying the foundation for their ongoing optimization, content iteration, and differentiated design tailored to different types of players.

The difficulty curve is the most critical aspect of this type of product, and William provided a detailed explanation: the beginner stage must be simple to help players build confidence, while the difficulty in the mid-game should increase gradually in steps to avoid a sudden, steep rise.When players get stuck, rewarded video ads are designed as an option for active assistance. Players can watch an ad to receive a hint or undo their last move, or they can simply retry—the choice is entirely up to the user.

The team monitors the number of retries and drop-off rates for each level. If the retry rate for a particular level is too high, they lower its difficulty. After several consecutive challenging levels, they also include bonus levels to give players a breather. As William puts it, “You can’t let players win all the time—they’ll get bored—but you can’t let them lose all the time either—they’ll quit.”A good difficulty curve makes players feel like they’re just a hair’s breadth away from passing, so they’re willing to try again.”

Simple, fun, and addictive

On the user acquisition side, paid user acquisition remains the foundation, but the bar for creativity has been redefined by short-video feeds. William noted that if players come across an ad and cannot understand the gameplay within three seconds, the conversion rate will naturally be low; products with such a high learning curve will directly lose the most fundamental basis for the spread of mini-games.

In terms of user retention, efforts to re-engage existing users are strictly segmented by tier; budget is allocated only for high-value users. Re-engaging casual, one-time players is costly and yields low conversion rates, so these efforts are typically abandoned.Reactivation efforts are also kept to a minimum, with outreach conducted only through platform-compliant channels during major version updates or the release of new large-scale level packs, complemented by return rewards to lower the barrier to re-engagement.At the same time, based on the historical activity patterns of returning users, we further refine segmentation and tailor the difficulty and pacing to each segment, continuously optimizing the gaming experience for returning users to enhance their long-term retention.

The team views the balance between advertising and user experience as a lifeline. William revealed that the company has strict internal rules: any changes to ad placements or frequency must be accompanied by simultaneous monitoring of ARPU and retention rates; if retention drops significantly, the changes are immediately reversed, and any changes aimed solely at short-term revenue growth are categorically rejected.

“Retention is the foundation of IAA products, while ad monetization is the result—we must not put the cart before the horse,” he said. He believes that some products increase ad impressions to boost ad revenue; while this leads to a short-term rise in revenue, retention eventually declines, causing overall LTV to drop instead. Many teams have miscalculated this balance.

03

What Makes a Casual Game a “Long-Running Hit”?

What exactly constitutes a timeless product? From the perspectives of the industry and manufacturers, the answer may vary slightly.

In terms of time, a mini-game must be in operation for two to three years or more—a lifespan comparable to that of a mobile game—to be considered an evergreen game. Of course, assessing the potential of a single title requires examining multiple factors, such as user base, user demographics, and operational metrics; each specific case must be analyzed on its own merits.

It’s worth noting that game mechanics follow cyclical patterns, and long-running products share a common trait: classic gameplay combined with subtle innovations.Whether it’s *Sheep Sheep*, *Pig Pig*, or the 2026 hit *Zhao Yun and A Dou*, all of these games build upon classic gameplay by introducing new mechanics or thematic elements, breathing new life into “old” games.Gameplay concepts long forgotten by history, though not currently popular, still have the opportunity to be reborn.

WeChat Mini-Game Advertising Landscape in the First Half of 2026

William’s analysis focuses more on data signals. He explained that the team looks for shifts in growth dynamics: when user acquisition no longer drives significant growth and revenue shifts toward repeat engagement from existing users, it signals that the product has entered its next phase. If new user retention continues to weaken over the long term, even if daily active users remain high, the product has effectively entered a period of decline.

Regarding failed products, Tongqu identified four common characteristics: gameplay that can’t be understood within three seconds; a core loop lacking immediate feedback; homogenized “skin-swap” designs with no memorable features; and gameplay that cannot be demonstrated through short videos.The criteria for discontinuing a product are equally clear: the core loop is disproved by data, the monetization model remains unsustainable over the long term, and there is no room for further iteration. Only when all three conditions are met will investment be halted, after which the product enters a maintenance phase involving server retention and the gradual shutdown of advertising campaigns. William added, “We won’t ax a product outright while there are still testable hypotheses remaining;and every time a product is shut down, the team must conduct a post-mortem.”

There are also some quiet long-distance runners in the industry.

For example, *Lie Flat and Level Up* is one such game. Launched in early 2022—even before *Sheep Sheep*—it has maintained its popularity long after its initial creative surge. With a user base primarily consisting of students and a low-key development team that rarely interacts with the media, it can truly be called a “hidden big boss.”

04

Policy Balance

The platform’s policies and capabilities form the other half of the environment in which Changqing Games thrives.

In August 2026, the platform rolled out a new round of upgrades to the IAA incentive program. For games where advertising is the primary revenue source, the duration requirement for users who registered or returned via Tencent Ads or external user acquisition channels was relaxed from “being active in the game for more than 5 minutes on the same day” to “having been active for a cumulative total of more than 3 minutes since registration.”

The platform explained that changing the metric from daily usage time to cumulative usage over time better reflects users’ actual activity patterns and helps bring more active users into the incentive program.

The duration of the long-term incentive program has been extended accordingly; the original “35% of ad revenue from days 1 to 90” has been adjusted to “35% of ad revenue from days 1 to 180.”Developers may choose between the “40% of ad revenue from days 1 to 30” light-to-moderate plan and the long-term plan. Products with longer lifecycles and stronger user retention capabilities will receive more substantial incentive support.

In addition, users who have been inactive for more than 45 days and return through eligible user acquisition scenarios—after reaching the required cumulative active time—are eligible for the same incentives as registered users. With lower time thresholds and a longer incentive period, the goal is to help developers refine high-quality products, strategically build long-term user retention, and achieve more stable returns.

At the same time, new tools and content formats are lowering the barriers to long-term success. This year, the platform launched a revenue diagnosis and optimization tool to help developers distinguish between the user acquisition distribution of core users, secondary core users, and casual users, and to provide industry benchmark data for comparison—enabling teams to determine whether the problem lies with the product itself or with their advertising strategy.

Mini-Game Revenue Diagnostic and Optimization Tool

On the content side, products such as *Eternal Night: Origins* are beginning to experiment with combining AI-generated animated series with mini-games, where the animated series is responsible for character development and attracting viewers, while the games handle conversion. This content strategy—which in the past only large companies had the resources to implement—is now spreading to small and medium-sized teams.

Of course, sharing via WeChat remains a long-term and effective way for WeChat Mini Games to acquire users. Today, developers are gradually shifting their focus from simply “setting up sharing entry points” to “designing the sharing experience,” ensuring that players are provided with content worth sharing at the exact moment they feel the urge to do so.In addition, the platform has introduced new social features such as head-to-head challenges and blue envelope gifting, using more interactive designs to boost sharing efficiency.

Recently, the show *The Ideal Life* leveraged a “platform social red envelope + sharing” mechanism, where both the sharer and their friends receive cash red envelopes. This approach ensures that sharing rewards drive genuine interaction. Compared to traditional user acquisition methods, the paid user penetration, new user acquisition, and retention rates among invited users are higher, resulting in better user quality and significantly improved ROI.

With Evergreen’s establishment, the next hurdle has already come into view.

“Sheep, Sheep” and “Catch the Goose” are prime examples of mini-games being turned into IPs; both titles have launched merchandise, participated in offline comic conventions, and have collaborated with JD.com.William revealed that Tongqu is already selling plush toys based on *Piggy Pig* and is exploring ways to integrate the game’s characters into animated series. He hopes that the Tencent ecosystem can provide more support in amplifying the IP’s reach.

Once the success of a few products—which was once a matter of luck—evolves into a proven, verifiable, and replicable model, the question of how to cultivate genuine IP and brand value will likely become an unavoidable challenge for mini-games as they enter this new phase.

title: When Ads Become Must-Watch Content: A Muscular Tang Seng Sings Rock, and AI Rewrites the Rules for Acquiring Users
text:
Recently, a batch of gaming-themed content has been drawing a loyal following eager for new updates. These videos feature neither celebrity endorsements nor in-game gameplay footage—just characters from the games pulling pranks.
For example, *Crazy Water World* features a bald, middle-aged man named “Fei Qiang” who repeatedly retrieves a seawater filter from the apocalyptic floodwaters, prompting viewers in the comments section to demand new episodes and create memes.
Also in Guangzhou, another small team of about 30 people is going through a similar experience. In their dark-themed, idle card game *Origin of the Eternal Night*, based on the *Journey to the West*, they’ve transformed Tang Seng into a muscular tough guy and had him sing in a video.This “Tang Seng singing” clip has garnered 7 million views on Video Account, with users requesting songs in the comments section—some even leaving messages saying, “If you make short dramas, I’ll definitely spend money on them.”
“In all my years of user acquisition, this is the first time I’ve seen users actively seeking out our ads,” said Liu Yi, the head of publishing for *Eternal Night: Origins*, with a touch of emotion. “Some users even started following our account because of the ads.”
Advertisements have traditionally been designed to interrupt content and prompt consumption. Today, some game ads have begun to take on the characteristics of content in their own right: viewers voluntarily linger, actively seek out new updates, and are subsequently directed to the game to complete a purchase.According to data from the DataEye Research Institute, *Origin of the Eternal Night* launched performance-based ad campaigns in early August 2026, with the daily volume of ad creatives—primarily AI-generated—at one point exceeding 10,000. The game entered the WeChat Mini Games Top Grossing Chart on its eighth day after launch, and its ranking continued to climb, reaching as high as fourth place.
01
Content-driven customer acquisition used to be very expensive
The gaming industry has been trying to attract players with content for nearly a decade, but the high barriers to entry in the past have kept most companies out of the market.
In 2017, in an advertisement for *Tanwan Blue Moon* released by Tanwan Games, Nick Cheung’s slurred line, “If you’re my brother, come cut me down,” unexpectedly went viral on social media and inspired a flood of fan-created content.At its peak, the game generated monthly revenue exceeding 200 million yuan, and its operator, Zhongxu Future, subsequently listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
According to Zhongxu Future’s 2022 IPO filing,from 2019 to 2021, its marketing and promotion expenses totaled 2.35 billion yuan, 1.643 billion yuan, and 3.739 billion yuan, respectively, accounting for approximately 78%, 57%, and 65% of revenue—with the figure approaching 80% in 2019.The reach of this type of advertising relies on celebrity influence and serendipitous online chemistry, making it difficult to plan and even harder to replicate.
Next came story-driven user acquisition content. Starting in 2019, the online money-making game *Sunshine Pig Farm* released a large volume of user-generated story content centered on cash-out features and red envelope giveaways, causing its user base to expand rapidly. Meanwhile, developers of “legendary” games experimented with situational dramas featuring a mix of celebrities and ordinary users.
In overseas markets, companies like Playrix have run “Save the Dog”-style narrative ads. Taking their game *Township* as an example, third-party ad tracking data shows that a narrative ad for *Township*—which ran from late 2021 to August 2022—generated an estimated 20 million impressions.While conversion efficiency has been repeatedly validated, the high costs and limited production capacity associated with live-action filming, as well as skepticism regarding discrepancies between ad content and actual gameplay, began to plague the industry during this period.
Later on, game companies began experimenting with full-fledged short dramas. According to publicly available information, in 2023, Caesar Culture partnered with Douyin’s short drama team to launch the mini-web series *The Road to Fighting Champion* for the mobile game *Battle Rules*; the first three episodes garnered a combined view count of over 20 million.In October 2024, *Fingertip Unrivaled* released a spin-off Three Kingdoms-themed short series and launched a live-action short series event within the game,allowing players to watch the series for free and unlock character content. However, given that the production cost of a single live-action short series ranges from hundreds of thousands to several million yuan, such productions are limited to serving as occasional marketing campaigns rather than a stream of daily-updated content.
“JUSTICE: A City of Contrasts,” a pinnacle of video game-derived content
Major studios, however, have taken this approach to a whole new level.According to Variety, citing sources familiar with the matter, the production and marketing costs for the two seasons (totaling 18 episodes) of the *League of Legends* spin-off animated series *Arcane* amounted to approximately $250 million, with the first season alone taking about six years to produce. Although the series sparked a craze, the high time and financial costs involved are enough to deter small and medium-sized studios from even considering such a project.
Looking back at this thread, it becomes clear that the idea of turning ads into content has long been proven effective. The industry’s bottlenecks have consistently centered on three engineering challenges: production costs, content output capacity, and the speed of data iteration. In early 2026, video generation models experienced a surge in development, simultaneously resolving all three constraints.
According to observations by the DataEye Research Institute, the peak daily volume of promotional content for *Origin of the Eternal Night* exceeded 10,000 pieces—a scale that would have been unimaginable in the era of live-action filming.According to DataEye’s *2026 First-Half AI Drama and Anime Data Report*, from January to May 2026, the domestic AI drama and anime market exceeded 22 billion yuan, and is expected to reach 40 billion yuan for the full year.
The platform ecosystem is also shifting toward small and medium-sized teams. According to official data from WeChat, the number of mini-game developers has exceeded 500,000, with 80 percent of them being small and medium-sized teams of fewer than 30 people. Over the past year, more than 80 mini-games have had over one million daily active users, and more than 300 products have generated quarterly revenue exceeding 10 million yuan.
“When there was a surge in video-generation models at the beginning of the year, we saw it as an opportunity for small teams to gain a competitive edge.”Liu Yi recalls that at the time, the products the team was running were generating limited revenue, AI tools were expensive to use, and the return on investment for creative assets fell short of expectations—yet the team persisted in investing. “We believed this was the right thing to do, so we just went ahead and did it. It was also because this experience built up the team’s capabilities that we later saw our first surge in popularity with *Eternal Night*.”
02
Get users to like the characters first, then have them pay for them
The strategy for *Eternal Night: Origins* can be broken down into a clear chain of reasoning: since characters are the core assets of a card game, the primary goal of advertising creative is to make the audience like the characters and, as a result, want to own them.
Liu Yi explained that during the project planning phase, the team had two requirements for the theme: it had to be accessible, and the characters had to be memorable. “Journey to the West” and “Romance of the Three Kingdoms” were two options with relatively low barriers to entry. The team further determined that true “dark-themed Journey to the West” card games were rare on the market, so they settled on this niche.Character design revolved around the theme of contrast: the traditionally perceived frail Tang Monk was reimagined as a tough guy with well-defined muscles. The team drew inspiration from the positive feedback received for similar characters on short-video platforms to finalize the design.
Subsequent campaign data showed that the Tang Seng creative performed significantly better than those featuring other male characters. Based on this, the team concluded that the user base was predominantly male and from lower-tier markets. Consequently, the direction for new characters was adjusted: male characters were designed to avoid being overly handsome, while female characters were styled to have a more mature, “older sister” vibe.
The female character Da Heitian unexpectedly went viral. Liu Yi said that the team has seen users mention her in the comment sections of other games, and users have specifically requested her appearance under their own content—her popularity has exceeded expectations.
Liu Yi has his own take on the relationship between content and conversion, which he describes as a shift in the consumption scenario.Simply displaying gameplay footage and urging users to spend six yuan to roll for a character won’t appeal to users who aren’t interested in this type of game—it may even cause them to resist. By framing it differently—telling users that the team is working hard to produce the show and hoping they’ll support the product while enjoying the show—the meaning of the payment shifts from a mere monetary transaction to a form of support for the content.
Da Hei Tian, a favorite among players and viewers alike
The main battleground for this model is WeChat Video Accounts. Liu Yi explained that, in addition to the short conversion path, user-driven sharing and organic virality within the WeChat ecosystem offer even greater value for the product’s long-term operation. After a video is published, a mini-game anchor can be embedded; when users scroll past the video, a link to access the mini-game appears in the lower-left corner.
The WeChat Mini Games team told Game Tea House that they view this type of advertising as part of the content ecosystem, believing that this content can drive user acquisition. The platform provides developers with non-game scenarios—such as Video Accounts, the Game Circle, and PC—to help them better serve users through text, images, and videos.
According to historical data from QuestMobile cited in a 2024 report by Guosen Securities, users aged 36 and older account for approximately 60% of Video Account users, while users in fifth-tier and lower cities account for 19.8%—a higher proportion than that of Douyin and Kuaishou during the same period.At the May 2026 Developer Conference, WeChat officials disclosed that WeChat Mini Games had over 500 million monthly active users, with males accounting for 53% and females for 47%; users aged 24 and under, 24–40, and 40 and older accounted for 10%, 50%, and 40%, respectively.
WeChat Mini-Games User Profiles
The primary paying audience for card-based games consists of middle-aged users with fragmented free time and disposable income; the user profile derived by Liu Yi’s team from advertising data largely aligns with this demographic.
Liu Yi revealed that, from the very beginning of the game’s launch, the team had been using both the Video Account’s “Heat” feature and Tencent’s Advertising Quality (ADQ) platform simultaneously. After creating some relatively high-quality content, their ad spend increased by 5 to 6 times, with a single video reaching a peak of 7 million views. “In terms of the overall Video Account platform, we ranked first on the monthly chart,” he said.
The platform is also actively courting these teams. According to official data released by WeChat, the platform provides 50,000 yuan in promotional funds for the initial launch of new games, and the revenue threshold for in-app purchases (IAP) in newly launched games that is exempt from revenue sharing can reach 50 million yuan. Over the past year, revenue from mini-game livestreams has grown by 239% year-over-year.A Video Account promotion team told Game Teahouse that they are helping developers navigate their initial advertising strategies through support measures such as cold-start assistance for new games.
The WeChat Mini Games Developer Conference held in May 2026 was themed “From Connection to Longevity.” Following the event, Product Director Li Qing told the media that 500 million monthly active users is approaching the industry’s ceiling, and the platform is shifting its focus toward optimizing the ecosystem structure and exploring the long-term value of content.
The Video Channel promotion team revealed that content-based creatives—which initially accounted for a small proportion—have gradually become the main driver of ad spend for mini-games on the Video Channel and continue to grow rapidly. Among the mini-game ad campaigns monitored by the platform, the average spend per post for AI-generated creatives is also higher than the average for standard creatives.
03
Advertising Is Starting to Shape Games in the Opposite Direction
The changes brought about by this model are most evident in customer acquisition efficiency.
On its eighth day after launch, *Origin of the Eternal Night* entered the WeChat Mini Games Best-Selling Chart, and its ranking continued to climb thereafter, reaching as high as fourth place at one point.Liu Yi admitted that the results took the team by surprise; the game ranked quite high from the outset, so the team subsequently expanded its advertising budget while ensuring it met the return-on-investment targets. Observations from the platform corroborated this experience; the Video Account promotion team also noted that content-based creatives performed significantly better in terms of engagement than traditional promotional materials, and registration conversion rates were on par with the market average.
There are concrete benchmarks for this efficiency improvement. Liu Yi explained that certain visuals, which previously required production using the UE engine and took half a month to a month to complete, can now be finished in one to two days with the help of AI, while maintaining the same quality as before.An industry survey by the tech media outlet “Chaping” revealed that the price for a single piece of traditional 3D advertising footage can range from 100,000 to 200,000 yuan, with production cycles starting at one or two weeks; AI has compressed this cycle to just one or two days.
Liu Yi also emphasized that AI is not without its costs. In addition to labor expenses, the cost of AI tools represents an ongoing additional expense, and the output of visual content is limited by the complexity of the script; for some complex scenes, it can take more than a day to complete a single shot, requiring the creation of each individual shot before they are assembled.
In the creative industry, the rule is that the gains from cost reductions rarely translate into profit; instead, they are mostly reinvested into advertising budgets and resources for trial and error.
A change even more profound than efficiency is taking place on the product side, where advertising data is beginning to influence game content. Iterations in card games rely heavily on new characters, and Liu Yi’s team provides feedback on each character’s advertising performance to the R&D team, which uses this as a basis for designing new characters. A prime example of this is how data on Tang Seng’s promotional materials led to the conclusion that the game appeals primarily to male users in lower-tier markets.
A Tang Seng Completely Different from the Traditional Image
Using user acquisition data to inform project initiation and product decisions is already common practice in the game publishing industry, and AI has significantly accelerated the validation process.Liu Yi explained that a character concept can be quickly visualized to test click-through rates and cost-effectiveness before the findings are shared with the R&D team. Another team member offered a more systematic explanation: there are no set rules regarding who proposes suggestions during the project initiation process; the key lies in who can provide data proving that users genuinely like it.
At the heart of business decision-making are investment costs, certainty, and expected returns—a process similar to that of filmmaking, where research, project approval, and production form a complete chain, and distribution and R&D share responsibilities based solely on feasibility and success rates.
User engagement is also evolving. As ads are constantly updated, some users have developed a habit of following the latest content, requesting songs in the comments section, and suggesting that characters try new musical styles.One user comment that left a strong impression on Liu Yi was, “If you make short dramas, I’ll definitely pay for them.” He interpreted this to mean that while users might not convert the first time they see an ad, consistently producing high-quality content will cause them to follow the account, thereby increasing the chances of conversion. The team views this type of user as a key source of growth.
Currently, the “Eternal Night: Origins” team operates five or six official accounts on Video Channel, with plans to have different accounts focus on different types of content, such as singing and story-driven content, and is considering launching character merchandise at the right time to reward users.
This model is already close to virtual idol management, and Liu Yi acknowledges that it has elements of that—in a sense, some of the characters have already “made their debut.” However, he remains cautious about whether to enter the short-form video industry directly. The product has been live for just over two months, and there are still many issues to address; with a limited team size, they need to focus their resources on resolving urgent matters.While the short-form video business may be explored in the future, at this stage, the content still serves to enhance the product’s distribution performance.
04
The Leveled and the Elevated
It is widely acknowledged in the game publishing industry that AI is leveling the playing field when it comes to content creation.
Liu Yi believes that while differences in production capabilities may be quickly bridged, differences in results will persist over the long term. Even with the same script, the quality of work produced by different designers varies significantly, due to differences in their aesthetic sensibilities and proficiency with prompts.
He illustrated the value of creativity using examples from the industry. “Crazy Water World” closely integrated source material with trending topics; the team created set props such as a seawater filter and an electric eel generator to serve as memory anchors. These anchors naturally align with the post-apocalyptic survival theme, allowing various trending topics to be incorporated into the concept.It is difficult for AI to directly produce this kind of design. If you simply feed trending topics to an AI and ask it to package them, the results are usually unusable; human insight remains the source of competitive advantage.
Opinions vary regarding the lifecycle of AI-generated content. Conclusions from academic experiments tend to be cautious, while several consumer studies have shown that, when participants are unaware, their evaluations of AI-generated ads are similar to those of human-created ads; however, once they learn that the content was generated by AI, their trust and willingness to purchase drop significantly.
However, frontline workers have a different experience.
Liu Yi believes that user fatigue stems from repetitive creative formulas, not from AI as a format itself; as long as creativity continues to evolve, the visual format itself will not easily grow tiresome.Another team member’s assessment was even more direct: most ordinary users cannot tell whether content is AI-generated or not. What industry professionals need to do is track changes in user preferences and respond with content that reflects those preferences.
In-Game Character Encyclopedia
The platform has adopted a more pragmatic approach. The Video Channel promotion team told Game Teahouse that while they support developers using tools such as AI to enrich their content, they do not encourage the mere pursuit of quantity or short-term exposure. Whether the interest generated by the content can be converted into sustained game engagement also depends on whether the gaming experience meets user expectations.
Liu Yi’s team’s strategy is to prepare for all possibilities. He mentioned that the company’s leader often says, “First determine right from wrong, then good from bad”—meaning they should invest in what they believe is right first and let the results unfold naturally.During the model boom in early 2026, even as returns fell short of expectations, the team continued to refine its AI content generation capabilities—an effort that ultimately paved the way for the product’s subsequent scaling on Video Account.
In Liu Yi’s view, once AI is integrated into workflows, creativity and quality actually become even more important than before—these are the two key factors for distributors to build a competitive edge.
When it comes to industry trends over the next one to two years, he remains cautious, reluctant to draw conclusions about specific categories. Instead, he emphasizes the value of user insights, believing that any category has the potential to succeed as long as it addresses user needs.His advice to newcomers to the industry also centers on building long-term assets: studying the platform ecosystem and content compliance, establishing an account matrix and community management system, and providing support for the long-term operation of their products.
