title: XBOX确认Project Helix是一款能运行电脑游戏的主机
author: Zeno Tong
text:
相关文章: XBOX公布25周年纪念开机动画
XBOX确认，Project Helix「被设计为一款能够运行你电脑上游戏的主机」。
微软出人意料地发布了《XBOX 25周年纪念杂志》，披露了大量有关其过去、现在和未来的细节。这都是为庆祝XBOX诞生25周年而举办的惊喜庆典的一部分，而这本杂志恰好也透露了比我们近来所获悉的更多的Project Helix相关信息。
XBOX首席执行官Asha Sharma此前曾将这个次世代项目称为一个「设备家族」，虽然这次再次使用了这一说法，但次世代业务副总裁Jason Ronald帮助人们更清楚地了解了它。这里的主要意思是，在XBOX历史的起伏中，团队吸取了许多经验教训。
Ronald说：「谈到Project Helix，它确实是按终极游戏设备设计的——一台能消除过去存在的所有游戏障碍的设备。我可以访问自己的整个游戏库。我能够随身带上跨越四代的XBOX游戏库和游戏进度，并立即使用。我们还消除了主机游戏和PC游戏之间人为设定的限制。」
对于Project Helix来说，这些承诺已经相当重大；有人猜测它最早会在2027年末推出，但它究竟是什么？目前还不知道我们何时能看到它所涵盖的设备家族究竟是什么样子，但今天，Ronald至少愿意向XBOX粉丝推介这个项目的理念：它似乎更侧重于传统意义上的主机，而非其他任何东西。
他补充说：「我们的设计目标非常明确：Helix被设计为一款也能够运行你电脑上游戏的主机。它不是一台也能玩主机游戏的PC。目标是让访问我的游戏变得简单、直观且即时。但如果你是硬核玩家或高级用户，希望对设置和性能选项进行更深层次的自定义，你完全可以这么做。」
不过，Ronald表示，多年来打造这个次世代项目并不只是回答当下的问题，也意味着要着眼未来。他没有直接说明这可能与这个神秘的XBOX项目有何关联，而是提到了阿尔法世代如何适应一个内容不被锁定在任何单一设备上的世界。他还谈到，他认为用户生成的游戏内容等事物的创作门槛在不久的将来「将会降低」，并表示玩家最终将「拥有大得多的自主权」和「对自身体验的控制权」。
这位Project Helix负责人还回顾了微软如何在XBOX One上「忽视了真正神奇的东西」。展望未来，一切都将围绕玩家、开发者以及他们热爱的游戏展开。
不过，无论Project Helix是什么、它能做什么或能运行什么游戏，有一件事比几乎其他任何事情都更重要：价格。游戏行业正受到一场零部件危机的冲击，这场危机已经大幅推高了享受游戏这一爱好的成本。随着从主机到存储设备的各种产品价格飞涨，通常弥漫在次世代升级即将到来之际的兴奋情绪已被恐惧取代。一些玩家甚至开始要求索尼和微软等厂商推迟新硬件计划，直到价格下降——或者至少等到他们能攒够钱。
外部形势严峻，但谈到Project Helix，Ronald仍持乐观态度。他甚至表示，当前的零部件危机促使团队迎接挑战。
他说：「这无疑是一个充满挑战的时期，但作为系统和平台设计师，这也是最令人兴奋的时期之一，因为我们必须发明全新的技术，才能继续推动尖端技术的发展，同时继续让产品易于获得、价格实惠。这是我们非常关注神经渲染等进展的一个重要原因，因为这是一种生成画面的全新方式，不需要更多计算能力、额外内存之类的东西。我认为，未来三到五年你将看到的创新会比过去10年更多。」 还有更多相关内容 XBOX 25周年促销礼包活动宣传视频
微软认为Project Helix是向下一代XBOX游戏主机的过渡。说到这一点，Ronald表示，游戏保存一直是并将继续是「XBOX的核心」。他和团队已经在着眼未来。他说：「（兼容性）确实影响着我们如何设计平台，以及我们如何与合作伙伴协作，以确保这些游戏不仅能够运行，还能在未来获得比以往任何时候都更好的游玩体验。我们不仅在保存过去的那些游戏，这实际上还影响着我们如今如何设计和打造平台及游戏——让它们在未来20年、30年后仍能保存下来。」
这篇XBOX杂志文章还将Project Helix称为「一个能够随你移动的平台上的皇冠明珠」。Ronald表示，这款设备的目标是「消除游戏障碍、消除阻碍，以及过去存在的那些人为设定的界限」。他解释说：「我们的设计目标是，无论你在哪里玩，体验都非常直观，并且具有鲜明的XBOX特色，但我们也希望针对屏幕的独特能力进行调整，不管那是你客厅里的大屏幕电视，不管你是在主机上玩，还是将游戏串流到掌机的小屏幕上，甚至是在PC上玩——在那里，信息密度更高，你有鼠标和键盘，操作也更精确。我们希望它给人非常熟悉的感觉，同时也能利用你实际游玩所用设备的独特能力。」
XBOX指出，最近发布的ROG XBOX Ally和XBOX模式预示了其前进的方向。它在这方面收到的反馈已经帮助Project Helix进一步铺平了道路，Ronald甚至表示：「我们将Ally视为我们正在用Helix打造的东西的先导——但它受到了我们为Helix制定的许多设计理念的影响。」
在XBOX筹备Project Helix之际，它正在结束忙碌而动荡的一年。Sharma在2026年最初几个月接掌业务，标志着新篇章即将展开，但影响数千人的裁员和关闭的游戏工作室，让许多人难以对未来抱有期待。Sharma在7月的一次情况更新中承认，微软的游戏品牌「并不健康」。

相关文章:XBOX公布25周年纪念开机动画

XBOX确认，Project Helix「被设计为一款能够运行你电脑上游戏的主机」。

微软出人意料地发布了《XBOX 25周年纪念杂志》，披露了大量有关其过去、现在和未来的细节。这都是为庆祝XBOX诞生25周年而举办的惊喜庆典的一部分，而这本杂志恰好也透露了比我们近来所获悉的更多的Project Helix相关信息。

XBOX首席执行官Asha Sharma此前曾将这个次世代项目称为一个「设备家族」，虽然这次再次使用了这一说法，但次世代业务副总裁Jason Ronald帮助人们更清楚地了解了它。这里的主要意思是，在XBOX历史的起伏中，团队吸取了许多经验教训。

Ronald说：「谈到Project Helix，它确实是按终极游戏设备设计的——一台能消除过去存在的所有游戏障碍的设备。我可以访问自己的整个游戏库。我能够随身带上跨越四代的XBOX游戏库和游戏进度，并立即使用。我们还消除了主机游戏和PC游戏之间人为设定的限制。」

对于Project Helix来说，这些承诺已经相当重大；有人猜测它最早会在2027年末推出，但它究竟是什么？目前还不知道我们何时能看到它所涵盖的设备家族究竟是什么样子，但今天，Ronald至少愿意向XBOX粉丝推介这个项目的理念：它似乎更侧重于传统意义上的主机，而非其他任何东西。

他补充说：「我们的设计目标非常明确：Helix被设计为一款也能够运行你电脑上游戏的主机。它不是一台也能玩主机游戏的PC。目标是让访问我的游戏变得简单、直观且即时。但如果你是硬核玩家或高级用户，希望对设置和性能选项进行更深层次的自定义，你完全可以这么做。」

不过，Ronald表示，多年来打造这个次世代项目并不只是回答当下的问题，也意味着要着眼未来。他没有直接说明这可能与这个神秘的XBOX项目有何关联，而是提到了阿尔法世代如何适应一个内容不被锁定在任何单一设备上的世界。他还谈到，他认为用户生成的游戏内容等事物的创作门槛在不久的将来「将会降低」，并表示玩家最终将「拥有大得多的自主权」和「对自身体验的控制权」。

这位Project Helix负责人还回顾了微软如何在XBOX One上「忽视了真正神奇的东西」。展望未来，一切都将围绕玩家、开发者以及他们热爱的游戏展开。

不过，无论Project Helix是什么、它能做什么或能运行什么游戏，有一件事比几乎其他任何事情都更重要：价格。游戏行业正受到一场零部件危机的冲击，这场危机已经大幅推高了享受游戏这一爱好的成本。随着从主机到存储设备的各种产品价格飞涨，通常弥漫在次世代升级即将到来之际的兴奋情绪已被恐惧取代。一些玩家甚至开始要求索尼和微软等厂商推迟新硬件计划，直到价格下降——或者至少等到他们能攒够钱。

外部形势严峻，但谈到Project Helix，Ronald仍持乐观态度。他甚至表示，当前的零部件危机促使团队迎接挑战。

他说：「这无疑是一个充满挑战的时期，但作为系统和平台设计师，这也是最令人兴奋的时期之一，因为我们必须发明全新的技术，才能继续推动尖端技术的发展，同时继续让产品易于获得、价格实惠。这是我们非常关注神经渲染等进展的一个重要原因，因为这是一种生成画面的全新方式，不需要更多计算能力、额外内存之类的东西。我认为，未来三到五年你将看到的创新会比过去10年更多。」

title: 据报道黄仁勋正与盟友商讨重返NVIDIA可能性
author: Zeno Tong
text:
相关文章: 随着黄仁勋从NVIDIA辞职，游戏业务的未来悬而未决
据报道，黄仁勋已与盟友讨论了可能重返NVIDIA担任首席执行官一事。就在几天前，他刚刚从NVIDIA辞职。
这家科技巨头相关事态错综复杂，而有关其中最新一起意外转折的消息来自Financial Times的一篇新报道。报道称，黄仁勋已与亲信私下讨论了他复职的可能性，与此同时，一些NVIDIA员工和硅谷各界人士正呼吁他回归。 还有更多相关内容 Sam Altman回应先前言论引发的批评
过去一周，NVIDIA因负面原因登上了科技界的头条。就在七天前，公司董事会宣布已对黄仁勋展开独立调查。这一举动足以震动任何一家公司，而对NVIDIA和黄仁勋来说，这只是一周的开始。几天后，纽约时报报道称，这位科技界领军人物还与公司医疗保健副总裁Kimberly Powell有染，后者直接向他汇报工作。同一天，路透社也发布报道称，他还与另一名员工有染。
随着这些报道出现、更多传闻开始流传，黄仁勋宣布辞职，但后续事态只让网上的议论更加热烈。科技界的其他巨头，包括亿万富翁Elon Musk和Epic Games老板Tim Sweeney，都公开呼吁他复职。现在，黄仁勋本人似乎也在考虑复职可能会是什么样。
黄仁勋的一名盟友解释道：「前沿实验室之外，科技界所有举足轻重的人都喜欢黄仁勋。」他还表示，硅谷领袖正在为黄仁勋回归组建一个「作战室」，希望获得白宫支持。这项行动成功的可能性尚不明确，但据说得到了黄仁勋的支持。
然而，如果他们继续推行让黄仁勋重返NVIDIA担任首席执行官的计划，事情不会容易。他几天前才从公司辞职，尽管有关任何被指婚外情的细节仍不清楚，但不可否认的是，他的公众声誉已经受损。一名推动他回归的盟友承认，「与下属有染是足以被解雇的过错」。
与此同时，NVIDIA已经在幕后积极寻找继任者。执行副总裁兼首席财务官Colette Kress目前正接替黄仁勋担任临时首席执行官。Financial Times报道称，公司董事会已经接洽Arm首席执行官Rene Haas，将他视为潜在继任者。

关键字： 动作、2D 平台
发行日期： 2026/11/16（暂无中文）
你会为了拯救所爱之人而背弃自己的信仰吗？在这款对经典复古动作游戏进行现代重塑的作品中，穿梭于充满横版动作、致命生物和残暴头目的黑暗哥特世界，展开激战。
要塞 vs 要塞（NebulArena）
关键字： 自走棋、策略、类 Rogue
发行日期： 2026/11/16（ 中文支持 ）
歼星巨炮零距离开火，超武装要塞跃迁对撞！孤悬太空，用流水线武装你的要塞，精巧布局每一处武装与组件,静待下一场死斗。敌方要塞骤然跃迁而来，巨炮齐射，激光撕裂星海，装甲层层崩裂。当炮火归于沉寂，两座钢铁堡垒轰然相撞，唯有胜者可以继续这场轮回死斗。
ScopeCreep
关键字： 增量、弹幕射击
发行日期： 2026/11/16（ 中文支持 ）
低语的火焰渴求灵魂。每一次献祭，你的意志都会变得更强。与幽魂战斗，收集它们的精华，满足那也许永不消退的饥渴，在这款短小、节奏明快的增量游戏中。
直到高塔崩塌（The Tower Must Fall）
关键字： 塔防、策略、模拟
发行日期： 2026/11/16（ 中文支持 ）
建造令人匪夷所思的高塔。保卫高塔，抵御源源不绝的围攻敌潮。看着高塔分崩离析，然后重建一座更坚固的高塔。
桌面喵喵猫树（Desktop Cozy Cat Tree）
关键字： 桌面伴侣、猫
发行日期： 2026/11/16（ 中文支持 ）

关键字： 塔防、策略、僵尸
发行日期： 2026/11/16（ 中文支持 ）
《Survivors Under Siege》将动作即时战略与塔防完美融合，打造极简战术体验。巧妙部署你的部队，抓住完美时机出击，抵御一波又一波的丧尸与变异体。
Train Goes Choo Choo
关键字： 火车、休闲
发行日期： 2026/11/16（暂无中文）
想歇一口气吗？让这款超治愈的旅行模拟器带你步入日本的静谧乡村。在摄影中解锁隐藏成就，或是随心播放、让沿途流动的风光陪伴你。买好车票，找个舒服的位置，尽情享受这趟旅程吧。
The Legend of the Crystal Revolver
关键字： 动作类 Rogue、平台游戏
发行日期： 2026/11/16（暂无中文）
《The Legend of the Crystal Revolver》是一款节奏明快的 Roguelike 平台游戏，注重流畅的移动、畅快的战斗以及令人望而生畏的挑战。游戏中既有待玩家掌握的独特技能，又有精心生成的关卡，再加上死亡始终如影随形的威胁，每次通关都能带来全新的体验。
喂食之器（Feed The Vessel）
关键字： 增量、挂机游戏、恐怖
发行日期： 2026/11/16（ 中文支持 ）
一款增量游戏：在数百光年的虚空中，让一位饥饿的神明始终吃饱。在培养缸里培育克隆体，将他们屠宰、焚烧以换取肉、血和灵液，升级飞船的各个站点，把引擎推入超载，抵达彼岸。
灵渡之境（Spirit Crossing）
关键字： 多人、放松、探索、建造
发行日期： 2026/11/17（ 中文支持 ）
来自《Cozy Grove》的制作团队：在柔和的云彩中滑翔，帮助迷失的灵魂，并设计高山之巅上你自己的家。在温暖的篝火旁结交陌生朋友，或与朋友一起在天空中悠闲地钓鱼，分享回忆。欢迎来到你这个奇异的新家。🏠🏔️

关键字： 牌组构建式类 Rogue、回合制
发行日期： 2026/11/17（ 中文支持 ）EA
《哈玛雷特》是一款剧情向肉鸽卡牌构筑游戏。玩家将在游戏中揭开堕落骑士团的秘密，见证烈火焚城的真相，探寻至亲失踪的谜底。驾驭古老遗物的力量，在湮灭边缘与恶魔对抗，改写末世命运。
Littlelands
关键字： 动作冒险、探索、温馨惬意
发行日期： 2026/11/17（暂无中文）EA
只要知道去哪里找，The Littlelands 就充满了等待你探索的奇特角色和神奇景观。对于像你这样爱探索、爱采摘浆果、爱寻找埋藏的宝藏、爱在这片土地上漫步的大头小家伙来说，每一刻都可能是一场史诗般的冒险。
Ridiculous Space Battles
关键字： AI 生成内容、自走棋、太空模拟
发行日期： 2026/11/17（暂无中文）EA
《RIDICULOUS SPACE BATTLES》是史上首款自动战斗游戏《Gratuitous Space Battles》的精神续作！经过十五年的等待，那些荒诞至极、毫无道理的太空战斗终于回归了。
Trees Hate You
关键字： 欢乐、低容错、步行模拟
发行日期： 2026/11/17（ 中文支持 ）

关键字： 增量、城市营造、资源管理
发行日期： 2026/11/17（ 中文支持 ）
《Clicky Islands / 点点岛》是一款融合了放置点击、城市建造与资源管理的独特游戏。你将扮演国王任命的总督，负责探索并开发岛屿，拓展未来的王国。
Here Comes the Horde
关键字： 自走棋、增量、塔防
发行日期： 2026/11/17（ 中文支持 ）
《群尸来压境》是一款放置类自走棋游戏，你将调动大批军队来保卫城堡，抵御不死尸群的来袭。挺过一波波攻击，解锁新战斗单位，获得强大技能，让千军万马占领你的屏幕吧。
Func Key
关键字： 策略、牌组构建、文字游戏
发行日期： 2026/11/17（暂无中文）
《Func Key》是一款拼写 Roguelike 牌组构建游戏，你的键盘就是牌组！你可以自定义键盘，将其打造成终极拼写机器，也可以通过打破规则的模组留下文字痕迹。拼写、构建、放松——这一切都伴随着键盘那令人舒缓的“咔嗒”声。
第二部分
下一部分明日送上！
html:
本周万众瞩目的《GTA6》（Grand Theft Auto VI）将在 PS5 和 XBOX Series 平台发售，Steam 上的新游戏数量也开始逐渐减少。本周还会迎来 Steam 的“自走棋角色扮演游戏节”，一起来看看有没有感兴趣的作品吧！

注：本系列文章的信息主要整合自 Steam 与 SteamDB 的即将发售列表，由于 Steam 支持手动输入日期及发售、同步不及时等原因，本列表可能会遗漏收录一些作品的发售信息。如果本周有您的作品或您喜欢的作品未被列出，欢迎直接评论补充链接～～

关键字：自走棋、迷宫探索

发行日期：2026/11/16（中文支持）

发行日期：2026/11/16（中文支持）

Code Market

关键字：商店管理、编程

发行日期：2026/11/16（中文支持）

服从我吧！最终抉择：路西法（Obey Me! Sinner's Choice: Lucifer）

关键字：视觉小说、恋爱模拟、黑暗奇幻

发行日期：2026/11/16（中文支持）

你的身份是审判官，而路西法则是被告人。 在这部暗黑浪漫视觉小说中，你将审问堕落天使，并决定他的命运。 等待你的会是救赎，还是毁灭——亦或是，更加危险的结局？

Motocross The Game

关键字：竞速、模拟、摩托车越野

发行日期：2026/11/16（暂无中文）EA

一款由车手打造、专为车手设计的超写实越野摩托车模拟器。将摩托车和车手作为两个独立的物理实体进行操控，可通过匹配系统或私人房间参与在线竞速，并在实时全球计时赛排行榜上挑战极限。辅助功能让新手能够按照自己的节奏学习。

title: Slay the Spire 2 has a new character in testing, and she's really quite busted
author: Harvey Randall
text:
Slay the Spire 2 has a new character—notably, a new character in testing —and as the patch notes themselves point out , that testing will very much be needed: "We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch."
I decided to hop into the beta branch myself and take her for a whirl, and—yeah, those changes'll have to come. The Fool's central mechanic is her bow and arrow—she can fire an arrow/shoot card to deal damage equal to the card's base damage plus her aim. So if a shoot card deals 15 damage and she has six aim stocked, she'll deal 21.
This is a little busted, because by default, the Fool has 6 aim already put in her bank. Her non-strike starter card, Foolish Shot, already deals a hefty 15 damage for just one energy. With aim, the first time she uses it, it deals a whopping 21 damage, which is a heck of a damage output for the Fool's first round of combat.
The saving grace here is that when a card that fires an arrow is used, that arrow becomes lodged in a target, who gains the Impale status. You can't play any more arrow-based cards until you either Dislodge (another game term, hence the proper nounage) an arrow with a card that dislodges, or until you have more than one arrow.
In my runs, I wasn't able to figure out the latter. But I really didn't need to, because I was one-shotting bosses the whole way up the spire. One card in particular, Repeat Shot, seems borderline broken. While it is a rare, it shoots a target for 20 damage (when upgraded) X times, plus your current aim.
Mega Crit Mega Crit With precious little setup, I was casually knocking (or should I say nocking) out around 78 damage on turn one just by having the card pop into my hand. Add even a little aim generation to your deck, and Repeat Shot solves single-target fights for you. By making them dead.
There are some other interesting mechanics, too, such as a trio of melodies you can activate and trigger other cards off of. Wah Blast, for instance, hits twice if you've got a Cho or Ki melody active. There's also Stretch, which gives you extra block on the usage of your next block card, Sadness, a status card that can be turned into Joy which gives you energy and card draw, and tarot cards via a power called Mythic Form.
Obviously, she's broken. I absolutely shouldn't be one-card tapping bosses on Act 1 just because I happened to first-turn draw into a single rare card. But she is already very fun, and I look forward to seeing what more balanced version of The Fool will look like in the full game.
Other than that, the testing branch now has two new modes: Blitz, a more bite-sized version where there's no map or gold, and Dread, which appears to be an Ascension+ mode for masochists. Could never be me.

title: YouTuber and comedian Ashens has 1,000 hours in Baldur's Gate 3 and reveals the worst retro game he's ever played: 'By the time you've hacked it to work, it's just no fun whatsoever'
author: Rick Lane
text:
Disk Cleanup
(Image credit: Future) Welcome to Disk Cleanup , our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?"
Stuart Ashen—better known by his YouTube persona Ashens—grew up on a diet of 8-bit games on consoles like the Atari 2600 and the Spectrum. The earliest PC game he recalls playing was Syndicate Wars on his first home-built rig—a Pentium 200 MMX machine housed in a server tower case: "I loved Syndicate . Hated Syndicate Wars. Never got on with it at all," he says. "Ended up giving it to a friend who loved it … I think I went on to Duke Nukem 3D or something."
A YouTuber since 2006, Ashens is known primarily for his reviews of weird and (typically not) wonderful food products on his main channel , which to date has 1.67 million subscribers. But he's also a regular critic and commentator on retro video games, both on his twice weekly Ashenscast Twitch stream (which also covers obscure TV and film), and in books like Terrible Old Games You've Probably Never Heard Of .
Alongside his video work, Ashens is currently making a folk horror film told in reverse. "Unfortunately, it's far enough away from release that there's no point plugging it," he says. But he hit pause on production to guide me through the haunted arcade of his PC. We talked DOS fighting games, the problem with rangers in RPGs, and the worst retro game Ashens has ever played.
What game are you currently playing?
(Image credit: Flaming Fowl Studios) I'm currently playing Gloomhaven , the digital version of the board game, for the second time. I put about 150 hours into it, then sort of left it, and I've come back to it.
It's kind of fantastic. I love board games, but Gloomhaven is one I didn't think I would ever play, because I know it takes two hours to set up or something. When the computer is taking control of all the bits and bobs, you can play it on your own in the background while you're doing other things and waiting for stuff. That’s going to get a lot of time from me.
It's all team-based. It's all your standard band of different [fantasy] archetypes together, and then after they reach a certain level, that's not true. When they do a certain personal quest thing, which can be a pain in the arse for various reasons, they retire, and then you can replace them with other ones you've unlocked. So the team basically changes, and the whole dynamic changes over time, which is something that's really kept me interested.
What was the previous game you played, and is it still installed?
(Image credit: Larian) The previous game would have been Baldur's Gate 3 , and it is still installed. I should uninstall it for two reasons. One, it takes up a lot of space, and two, I might start playing it and it will eat all my spare time again. Because, yeah, I got kind of obsessed.
To give you an idea, I'm now on 350 hours on Gloomhaven, but 927 on Baldur's Gate. Probably a good 50 to 100 hours of that is just sitting in the background [but] it's so far ahead of any other game I've played in terms of hours, it's unbelievable.
I've never played a Larian game [before], and I didn't like the early Baldur's Gate games. I got the first one free with a graphics card. I remember opening the graphics card box and about 14 discs fell out. I was so excited to play it and I could not get on with the combat. It was that weird, sort of issue commands and pause and do things. It just didn't do anything for me, and I thought, "Oh, that's disappointing." After a couple of hours, I never came back to it.
And then I saw something about Baldur's Gate 3—because I wasn't interested in it at all for obvious reasons, and it just had that spark to it of, "Hang on, there's something special going on here, with the writing of that." And then I saw they changed the combat to turn based, and I was like, "Right, sign me up."
I bought it, installed it, started playing it, and that was the only thing I played probably for two and a half, three years.
What is the oldest game (by release date) currently installed on your PC?
(Image credit: Capcom) This isn't one I played a lot—we have this because we were streaming it. But it's Street Fighter for DOS from 1988.
It's entirely different to the arcade version, I think it's got more in common with the weird Commodore 64 version. But basically, we were going through, on stream, every single DOS fighting game, and it's pretty bad. But weirdly, not as bad as a lot of them.
DOS fighting games are, like, for every good one, there's five really bad ones and one that you can't believe they'd charge money for. It barely works. I love fighting games, so it's always interesting to see these obscure ones we haven't heard of. But God, the DOS ones! It was like they saw Mortal Kombat but absolutely did not understand Mortal Kombat. So you've just got teenagers dancing around in front of a camcorder, badly digitised, and some Christ-awful game engine that just does not work fundamentally.
Then again, the arcade game is awful for the first Street Fighter. There's just not really much of a game to it. Even in the arcade, it's all about learning the special moves and repeating them over and over. Or trying to, because the controls are not quite there for Street Fighter 1. I think that's got to be one of the biggest improvements in history, from Street Fighter 1 to Street Fighter 2.
What is the highest number of hours you have in any given game, according to Steam?
(Image credit: Larian Studios) That is Baldur's Gate 3, with 927 hours.
I think I [initially] did a Ranger. I'm always interested in Rangers in RPGs, because they're never implemented very well. In EverQuest , it was the [class] that could dish a lot of damage and yet couldn't take any. It was just noticeably inferior …. It felt better in Baldur's Gate 3. It probably wasn't the optimal build, but it did actually work. I do like the ranged bow combat, and I'm always interested in why they never get it right. Is it just nobody likes Rangers, but they feel they have to put them in anyway?
I didn't go Dark Urge until the second playthrough, not really understanding what it was at the time, obviously. And then I was informed after, "Oh, you should try that." And I'm like, "Oh, this is what the game was written for. OK, yes, it's even better now."
It's absolutely incredible. Writing, performance, everything is a step above anything that had come before, I think. And the combat is so much fun, which obviously is super important because that's a huge percentage of it.
What game will you never, ever uninstall?
(Image credit: Electronic Arts) That is Command & Conquer 3: Kane's Wrath. Because sometimes, if I've got 10 minutes spare, I'll just quickly start up a skirmish map on it, just a simple 1v1, and see how quickly I can win, and that's it. It's almost a comfort thing. I only do it once maybe every couple of months, but I'll always leave it installed for that reason. Plus, by today's standards, it doesn't take up much room.
I think I like the skirmish better in 3, due to the variety of all the bits and bobs in it. It's probably not the tightest of the games in the series. But for me, that's the one I always enjoyed the most.
What's a piece of non-gaming software installed on your PC that you simply couldn't live without?
Everything .
There's a little window, and you type in the name of any file on your PC, and it's already indexed them, and it instantly appears with where they all are, and you can easily narrow things down. Life changing. The amount of files I've given stupid names to, or put in the wrong folder that I've just found immediately because of this. It's fundamentally changed the way I work.
How tidy is your desktop screen?
Oh dear. So I have icons turned off on the desktop. I'm going to turn them back on, if I can remember how.
Fuck! I'm turning that off. Oh no, that's not good. That's pretty bad. Oh God! How do I turn them off? Oh God, it's horrible.
It's just two 4k monitors entirely covered in icons and stuff. Because I don't use the desktop at all, so I just let it auto install things there and forget about it. I've got a little program called RocketDock , which keeps the useful things on the side of one of the monitors, and that's it. I've not looked at the actual desktop in years, and it is monstrous.
BONUS QUESTION: What's the best retro game you've discovered, and what's the worst retro game you've ever played?
(Image credit: Mindscape) One I only briefly played back in the day, and then something made me play it again on stream, and it was so much better than I remembered, [is] Moonstone for the Amiga. It's like a hack 'n' slash-y, brawler type thing, but with a lot of RPG elements. It's also beautifully designed, with really nice artwork and sound. But it's a really interesting game. No other game quite has the vibe of it. Not to say it's the best game ever or anything, but it's still very bloody good.
What is the worst overall? Oh man, there's so many bad ones. There's one called, which we keep talking about [on stream], Graeme Souness Vector Soccer . This isn't the worst. I'm just going to mention it because it's great. It's an Amiga game, and literally the characters are vectors. But of course, due to the way they didn't really have the processing power back then, these vectors look like the Keep Britain Tidy logo. So they're all weird things moving around and the frame rate is monstrous. It's like three frames a second. It's totally unplayable. Nobody seems to know if there's a good game under the hood or not.
I think for absolute worst, it's got to be SQIJ ! And it's for the Spectrum. There are versions for other computers that are perfectly competent. But the Spectrum one was written by a man, or a boy at the time, bless him, called Jason Creighton, who really didn't want to fucking write it or work at that company again. So he just spat out something absolutely awful that basically is borderline unplayable, sent it to them, and they just didn't bother looking at it. They just loaded it, went 'Oh, that loads.' Put it on tape, out it goes.
Powerhouse, the company that released it, released it twice—a standard release and then a release later on as a compilation. As released, it doesn't work. Basically, Jason accidentally turned on the caps lock or something in the source code, and you can't turn it off, and the keys actually don't function if caps lock is on. So you load it up and you can't move. That's it. Fortunately, it's so badly put together you can literally break into the program and turn the caps lock off through poking a memory access directly, if you know what I mean. And by the time you've hacked it to work, it's just no fun whatsoever.

title: The pandemic was transformative for Jackbox: 'We went from a gamer name to a household name'
author: Justin Wagner
text:
It's no secret that the Covid-19 pandemic saw a lot of people using videogames to stave off lockdown blues, and the Jackbox Party Pack games were especially well-suited for the role: easy-to-understand party fare that's optionally family-friendly and easy to play over a video call. PC Gamer said as much back in March 2020.
In a recent interview with PC Gamer associate editor Ted Litchfield, Jackbox Games CEO Mike Bilder said that the pandemic proved transformative for the developer.
"The industry at large obviously saw a lot of success at that time, but we did as well, and we went from a gamer name to a household name," he said, noting it was an "unfortunate period of time for the world, but for the gaming industry, a good one, and for Jackbox, a good one as well."
"That was kind of a leveling up for Jackbox as a company," said Bilder. "Suddenly office workers are doing happy hours and families over weekends are connecting over a game of Quiplash or something because it's what you did when you were locked down. People realized how easy it was to just share the screen over a Zoom call and everyone's playing."
It surprised employees at the studio to see how popular the games had become.
Chief marketing officer Brooke Hofer recalled a scene in the 2022 Knives Out sequel Glass Onion, where characters could be seen playing Quiplash over a Zoom call: "I remember when we all saw that in the studio, and we're like, 'Whoa,' you know. But that was so many people's experience at that time, and it was cool how that was captured in pop culture in various ways."

title: League of Legends will get an overhaul called New Dawn with new visuals, build options, and an updated client
author: Justin Wagner
text:
Riot has announced a League of Legends overhaul that promises to touch every aspect of the game.
"We want League to stand the test of time and be a game that's here for many years to come," said League Studio head Andrei "Meddler" van Roon in a teaser trailer . "And there are a lot of things that need to be true to make that happen."
The headlining changes coming with the update, called New Dawn, are a "modernized" client, a graphical revamp for the 5v5 map Summoner's Rift (the last time this happened was in 2014 ), and "new ways to play" each champion.
While details are scarce in the teaser, some brief footage is shown where you can see what he's talking about: a Blitzcrank player selects what looks like a character-specific mastery tree labeled "God Hand," and it cuts to him beating up an enemy in melee. Other champions are shown using abilities in ways they currently can't—Vayne, for instance, dashes through a wall.
An updated art style is also shown off, including new character models for all sorts of champions as well as bosses like Baron Nashor and the Elder Dragon. It looks much more in line with the art style of Wild Rift, League of Legends' mobile port-slash-spinoff with high-detail character models.
Player reactions are, as you might expect with an update that promises to be so comprehensive, all over the map.
"Am I the only one who thinks this looks like a mobile game," said Reddit user lukesherboiii in a thread sharing the trailer.
"I don't understand how anyone thinks this looks like a mobile game," said user OneSketchyWorld said in the same thread . "Like I know change can be hard for some, but I'm gonna hold off on judging it until I actually play it."
Riot also recently announced that its brand new League of Legends Classic mode failed to catch on, and will come to an end in January.

title: Are you more of an ambient music enjoyer or theatrical atmosphere appreciator?
author: Mollie Taylor
text:
When World of Warcraft: Forever's beta first launched, I lamented its long stretches of silence and penchant for ambience over theatrics. I still sort of stand by that, but after spending more time in Azeroth (and discovering the loop music setting) I've a new-found appreciation for both WoW's soundtrack and ambient music as a whole.
It's also got me thinking about what makes a soundtrack ambient versus something more melodic. I'm chronically Final Fantasy 14-brained, where just about everything has a grand thematic soundtrack to it—the jauntiness of the Gold Saucer, the soothing Middle-earthness of Gridania's outer Shroud zones, the grand organs of Ishgard's bitterly cold landscape. You can't escape composer Masayoshi Soken's penchant for leifmotifs. He will turn anything into an orchestral spectacle.
I'm a big JRPG fan in general, a genre I think is the absolute master of thematic soundtracks. But I also think fondly of games I've played over the years that are a little more pared down, their soundtracks there for a little atmosphere rather than actively driving the narrative. Minecraft's OST is a masterclass in ambience, and is in regular rotation across my videogame-themed Spotify playlists. I also have a huge soft spot for the soundtrack behind Mirror's Edge—one which settles in this almost otherworldly ambiance, only ramping up when Faith is in a perilous situation.
But what about you? Do you prefer the more subtle nuances that an atmospheric soundtrack has to offer? Or do you like your videogame music loud, in your face, and full of dramatics? Be sure to leave a comment and let me know which one's your favourite and why.

title: Influential Warhammer miniature designer Aly Morrison has died
author: Jody Macgregor
text:
Miniature designer and artist Aly Morrison has died, as confirmed by Trish Carden Miniatures and Design on Facebook . Carden, Morrison's ex-wife and former partner in Marauder Miniatures, posted that, "Mharaid and I are heartbroken to announce the passing of Aly Morrison, a very much loved father, veteran wargames miniatures designer and friend to many around the tabletop and the world. Aly passed unexpectedly but peacefully this Wednesday, and will be sorely missed."
Aly Morrison began sculpting for Citadel in 1983 as a freelancer before joining the studio full-time in 1986. He and Trish were then made stewards of Games Workshop's imprint Marauder Miniatures in 1988, where they had free reign to create quirky and characterful figures like the mohawked dwarf trollslayers and the giant with a whaler's beard and a booze barrel strapped to his waist that became archetypal parts of Warhammer.
Morrison also crafted the first miniatures for Blood Bowl players and drew the tokens to represent them in the board game's first edition. During his time at Games Workshop every faction from dark elves to space marines eventually benefited from his touch.
He's also well-regarded as a painter, and his reliance on a dark wash with a hint of purple in it jokingly known as "Aly's Brown Liquid" was legendary. He continued working on the recipe over the years, with a recent iteration described on his blog in 2020 if you want to whip some up yourself.
Though Marauder was eventually folded back into Citadel, Morrison continued at Games Workshop until his retirement earlier this year. The company remembered him by saying , "Aly’s kindness and generosity as a mentor have left an indelible mark on the Warhammer Studio. Humble, magnanimous and with an incorrigible wit, to sit beside Aly and hear his wisdom and love of Warhammer miniatures design, was to be in the presence of a master. No matter your level of experience, he always had something insightful to add, to help make the creation 'more Warhammer'."

title: The latest SteamOS update improves support on Nvidia-powered PCs: makes swapping your rig to the OS less painful
author: James Bentley
text:
The preview version of SteamOS 3.10.0 has just dropped, and with it comes better support for AMD and Nvidia hardware, and it's now based on Linux kernel 7.3.
For AMD graphics, the latest SteamOS update adds support for HDMI 2.1 VRR (Variable Refresh Rate), FRL(Fixed Rate Link), and ALLM (Auto Low Latency Mode). This should all contribute to a smoother gaming experience with higher bandwidth video and less input lag.
As for Nvidia graphics, it has reportedly received increased stability and performance, alongside support for Mesh Shaders on Turing and newer architectures. The latest SteamOS updates also fixed rendering corruption issues in Shadow of the Tomb Raider and The Surge 2.
Then, of course, SteamOS now uses the Linux 7.3 kernel (which launched last month).
Those are the big updates from SteamOS 3.10.0, but there are also a handful of fixes and changes. Game Mode has had the following changes:
Added support for VK_EXT_present_timing
Added support for ASUS ROG Xbox Ally X20 HDR and brightness adjustment
Improved frame timing when using the framerate limiter with VRR
Improved screen flickering when VRR is enabled while navigating the Steam UI or leaving it idle
Improved cursor movement under VRR. It should now match the game's framerate over 30 fps, and stop spiking the panel's refresh rate up to the maximum refresh rate
Fixed scaling causing overexposure in certain HDR titles, such as Control
Fixed an issue with certain games, such as UBOAT and The Fruit of Grisaia, where the image would flicker and present stale frames in Game Mode
SteamOS Previews are experimental by nature. You have to swap your update channel in Steam settings to get access, and there's always a chance new updates come with bugs or stability problems. If you come across a problem, Valve has a form to track SteamOS bugs.
If you don't fancy downloading a preview, SteamOS 3.10.0 is likely to come to the public channel at some point in the future, based on feedback from the preview.
Still, greater support for different hardware is good for wider SteamOS adoption, especially Nvidia kit, as that's always been a pain, and should make gaming on the Steam Machine and handhelds a little better.

title: WoW: Forever's continued to wrestle with dungeons, as Blizzard admits it briefly 'missed the mark' on hotfixes over the weekend
author: Harvey Randall
text:
World of Warcraft: Forever 's been pretty great. At this point, I have around 150 hours played, a terrible posture problem, and a level 47 warrior I just barely avoided doing a 2 am Zul'Farrak run with yesterday. Speaking of, there has been a point of contention: Dungeons.
My position on the debate is fairly neutral —I think you could maybe bump up the mob XP by around 10% as a compromise—but overall I think they're fine. The new ones are bangers, and I get a huge bunch of XP from doing them at least once. Blizzard's recent choices, however, did have me scratching my head over the weekend.
For a short time, via a hotfix , enemies in dungeons wouldn't give experience points to anyone in the group if they were trivial (that is, greyed out) to at least one party member. On paper, this sounds incredibly reasonable. WoW has suffered from a plague of dungeon boosters (that is, people selling runs of dungeons to let folks AFK through their levelling journey) particularly in Classic.
But the moment you take a second to stare at how Classic dungeons are designed, you start to see the cracks form. Uldaman, for instance, has a level range of 41-51 in my dungeon finder. Maraudon, 46-55. Then there's the issue of the Scarlet Monastery, whose entire gauntlet runs from level 30 to 44 and is often done in one big sweep by groups.
In other words, it was possible to be maybe a couple levels over the recommended range for a dungeon—which is certainly a great help, but I don't think can be counted as a boost —and ruin the already-diminished XP gains for everyone. Which is counter-intuitive in a game that's meant to be social.
To Blizzard's credit, its devs did spring into action on Saturday, amending the hotfix : "Yesterday, we updated dungeon play so that experience granted by an enemy in an instance is nullified if a high level player is in the group and enemy is trivial to that player. For some dungeons, the new restriction missed the mark because of the overall level range of the enemies in the dungeon.
"With hotfixes that are now live, we’ve just deployed a further change to this restriction, making it so that the XP nullification only kicks in when the high-level player is more than 12 levels above the level of the enemies."
To me that's more than reasonable. I don't think, say, a level 25 character coming to help their mate out with Deadmines should be ruining the XP gains for everybody else—sure, their presence makes the dungeon a heck of a lot easier, but so does grouping up for quests in the open world. 12 levels seems a fair compromise.

title: Jensen Huang reportedly eyeing up return to Nvidia as friendly tech execs form 'war room' to fight for him and over 175,000 people sign #bringjensenback petition
author: Jacob Ridley
text:
Jensen Huang stood down from his role as CEO of Nvidia on November 12. It's November 16 and 175,000…176,000…177,000 people have signed a petition to bring him back. Moreover, it is said the leather-clad man himself is considering a campaign to be reinstated at the helm of Nvidia, and some silicon valley execs are reportedly getting behind him.
There's even a hashtag for the campaign, which feels like a remnant of a lost age when those were actually good for something: #standwithjensen
In an open letter to the Nvidia board, the campaigners ask to "bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts, unless and until you can provide compelling evidence that his removal is in Nvidia's best interests."
The letter lays out three demands:
Reinstate Jensen as CEO
Ensurance an independent investigation and a fair hearing
Provide a timely public explanation
The Nvidia board has started an investigation into the events that led to Jensen Huang's resignation. If you've been living under a rock, those are: alleged affairs, one of which is said to be with someone suspected of being a Chinese spy, though heavily debated; and questions over smuggling cases and national security risks.
The board has hired legal firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to carry it out under the pretense of it being independent, and Huang had agreed to cooperate with it before his resignation. There's no promise of findings of that investigation being public, however, isn't enough for the signatories of the standwithjensen campaign.
The campaign admits that it cannot verify the roles or affiliations of those claimed to have signed the petition, so take the figures with a pinch of salt; however, it claims nearly 9,000 current employees of Nvidia have signed it, which for a company of just over 40,000, is around 20% of the business. Some big names claimed to have signed the document are Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney (who has been very vocal about his thoughts on the matter), Binance co-founder Yi He, and seemingly many other founders, CEOs, execs, and researchers.
Further to this, the Financial Times is reporting that Huang has been discussing the possibility of returning with confidants; presumably not very reliable ones as "people familiar with the matter" are cited in the report, unless they want it to get out, of course. One Huang ally reportedly told the FT it was setting up a "war room" to lobby for the CEO's return and get him back in the good books with US lawmakers.
(Image credit: Erik Flyg/Bloomberg via Getty Images, Nvidia) It wouldn't be an unfamiliar play for a major figure to resign following a scandal with a view to make a return at a later date. Politicians do it regularly enough; UK housing secretary Angela Rayner resigned from Keir Starmer's government following a report that said she broke the Ministerial Code, only to return to the same role under Andy Burnham.
Huang would have a tough path back to leadership. It's not just Nvidia's board that would need convincing, as US lawmakers are set to ask some tough questions of the guy as he joins a few committees in Congress in coming weeks. The outcome of which could either nail shut any chance of return for the ousted CEO, or open the door.
Even if Huang did make it back into the halls of Nvidia's offices, Endeavor and Voyager, in Santa Clara and, one must presume, the leather chair he left in his office, he wouldn't win the prize for shortest leave of absence.
(Image credit: Kyle Grillot/Bloomberg via Getty Images) Sam Altman was booted from OpenAI by the board due to a lack of faith in his leadership, and only five days later he was reinstated. Most of OpenAI's employees threatened to resign at the time, though there weren't many of them in total at the time, and a few key people left immediately. That did well to push for his re-hiring , which will surely be something any allies of Huang will have in mind as they build a case for his return.
Steve Jobs was famously ousted from Apple, too, though it took him years to return; he got back when Apple bought his company NeXT, which later went on to form the foundation for every MacBook. So if Huang just builds another company with an even better product, he'll be back in no time.
Nvidia, meanwhile, is reportedly set to be designated one of the United States' "national champions" , which the Trump administration is said to be hoping will help win foreign business. Speaking of the US president, Trump had backed Huang before he resigned, but quickly moved on to recommend Apple's Tim Cook as a suitable replacement.

title: New Asus beta BIOS patches now include a fresh AMD feature to stop you thinking your PC's b0rked
author: Dave James
text:
Memory training is boring stuff. Your PC will spend an age running through it when you first boot your PC, or you swap in some new RAM sticks (lucky you), or you make a change which has anything to do with memory in your BIOS. Or just because your PC decides it might fancy doing it again. But a new AGESA 1.3.0.1F beta BIOS update, first from Asus (via Uniko's Hardware ), has made this whole process a lot more exciting.
Well, going from not at all exciting to something is always going to feel like a bigger deal, but I don't necessarily want to oversell it. Though when you're waiting for memory training to complete it's real nice to at least have a readout to indicate that it is progressing and your PC hasn't just hung.
This is the issue with memory training on PCs in the past. It was pretty damned opaque, in that you'd start up your PC and it would do… nothing. The fans would spin up, and the lights would light, but you'd have no readout on your monitor, and the debug screen on your motherboard would just have a static figure. Mine would be stuck on '15' for an age.
Obviously you could just go looking up the error code and it would inform you that your system was just having a good long think about its system memory, but if you didn't know that could be a thing, it can feel like your rig is bricked.
The new AGESA 1.3.0.1F beta patches are out now, first from Asus, but you can bet other motherboard vendors will be following suit soon enough. This latest version of the AGESA BIOS brings with it AMD's new memory training function, which shows on the motherboard's debug screen that the memory training process is, indeed, proceeding. You'll see it tick up, first from 00 to 09, and then it will go through 0a, 0b, 0c, etc. to show that it is working through the memory training and that it isn't stuck.
You're still getting nothing on your monitor screen, however. The memory training function is done well before your system gets around to turning on your rig's GPU.
My Asus Crosshair X870E Hero board, with 64 GB DDR5-6000, and a Ryzen 9 9950X, went all the way up to 11 (cue guitar riff) before the training was complete and the motherboard rebooted happily.
This means you'll immediately see if it is stuck, so no more waiting around for 15 minutes to actually go, 'okay, yeah, this is screwed right here'.

Memory training is boring stuff. Your PC will spend an age running through it when you first boot your PC, or you swap in some new RAM sticks (lucky you), or you make a change which has anything to do with memory in your BIOS. Or just because your PC decides it might fancy doing it again. But a new AGESA 1.3.0.1F beta BIOS update, first from Asus (via Uniko's Hardware), has made this whole process a lot more exciting.

Well, going from not at all exciting to something is always going to feel like a bigger deal, but I don't necessarily want to oversell it. Though when you're waiting for memory training to complete it's real nice to at least have a readout to indicate that it is progressing and your PC hasn't just hung.

This is the issue with memory training on PCs in the past. It was pretty damned opaque, in that you'd start up your PC and it would do… nothing. The fans would spin up, and the lights would light, but you'd have no readout on your monitor, and the debug screen on your motherboard would just have a static figure. Mine would be stuck on '15' for an age.

Obviously you could just go looking up the error code and it would inform you that your system was just having a good long think about its system memory, but if you didn't know that could be a thing, it can feel like your rig is bricked.

The new AGESA 1.3.0.1F beta patches are out now, first from Asus, but you can bet other motherboard vendors will be following suit soon enough. This latest version of the AGESA BIOS brings with it AMD's new memory training function, which shows on the motherboard's debug screen that the memory training process is, indeed, proceeding. You'll see it tick up, first from 00 to 09, and then it will go through 0a, 0b, 0c, etc. to show that it is working through the memory training and that it isn't stuck.

You're still getting nothing on your monitor screen, however. The memory training function is done well before your system gets around to turning on your rig's GPU.

This latest update is then a pretty small thing for AMD users only, and minor news in the wider world of a reeling tech industry and a market where doing anything to the memory in your rig is almost wishful thinking today, but as a wee quality of life upgrade, and as an AMD CPU user, I'm certainly here for it.

But it's worth noting these are beta BIOS updates, and that comes with some risks that you probably don't need to take in order to get this extra feature. My current official BIOS is AGESA 1.3.0.1d, but I've tested out the new 1.3.0.1f Patch A BIOS from this ROG Forum link. If your rig's running just fine right now, I'd probably suggest sticking with the latest non-beta patches.

title: Intel hit with class action alleging it 'misled investors' – company's recent downturn due in part to how darn expensive PCs are right now
author: James Bentley
text:
Hot on the heels of a monumental share price drop for the company, Intel now faces a class action lawsuit from its own shareholders.
This is according to an alert from law firm Robbins LLP , which recently informed all investors. This suit alleges "Intel misled investors about demand for its products and the Company's future growth potential."
The class action can involve anyone who bought stock between July 23, 2026, and October 29, 2026, known as the "class period".
With the memory crisis in full effect, PC sales are down worldwide ( estimated to be 20% down in October ), but the lawsuit argues that the PC sales slowdown was "having a materially greater negative impact to Intel’s third quarter 2026 Client Computing and Physical AI Group results than defendants had disclosed to investors."
It also argues Intel's OEM and distribution partners were left with hardware they couldn't sell to consumers due to rising prices, and that positive impacts of Intel business coming from the AI boom were off "more than offset by the negative effects on the Company’s business and financial results resulting from the PC market slowdown and the excess inventory buildup."
(Image credit: Intel) The suit also alleges that Intel's reporting of its operations and ability to capitalise on the AI boom "were materially false and misleading when made, and such statements did not accurately reflect Intel’s then-present business and prospects."
With Robbins LLP informing investors of this class action lawsuit, it's possible more could join the claim, and we don't actually know how many are currently in the class action right now. The law firm notes that those who purchased stock in the class period have until January 12, 2027, to join.
It's important to note that Intel stock prices have dropped significantly, declining by 29% at the end of the last month, and upwards of 40% in the last six months. From $95.53 per share on Wednesday, October 28, to $59.66 per share as of the time of writing, that's a 38% decline. To a shareholder, that is a straight devaluation of however much money they would have put into the company in that period.
Intel has had its fair share of ups and downs over the last few years. With a long history behind it, Intel made a killing in the '90s and '00s, becoming a market leader for CPUs, but unstable chips and underperforming chips marked a downward trend for the company. This is all while TSMC has surpassed it in chip manufacturing and AMD has managed to pull ahead in the gaming CPU market. The decline in PC sales thanks to the memory crisis only made things worse for Team Blue.
Intel doesn't appear down for the count, with it gaining market share from AMD just last week (and its recent handheld chips are excellent ). Still, some of Intel's own shareholders alleging they've been misled is certainly not a great look for a company that is still very much on its way back up.

title: 'Game dev isn't always straightforward': Overwatch's director responds to players upset about season 6's hero being a DPS
author: Elie Gould
text:
Last week we found out a few new things about the next hero coming to Overwatch in season 6. He's an omnic detective, his name's Hudson , he has a fun accent, and he will be a DPS. Hudson is the last hero to be released from the batch teased earlier this year during Overwatch's Spotlight , and after all this time I'm very excited to see what he has to offer. But not everyone shares this sentiment.
There's a good chunk of players who are upset about Hudson, before they've even tried him out, simply because he's not a support hero, which was what Team 4 initially promised him to be. I've seen this discontent online and honestly ignored it, thinking it was either bots or people farming for attention because I cannot fathom why anyone is honestly upset about this.
(Image credit: Blizzard Entertainment) I've been maining support in Overwatch for almost 10 years now, ever since open queue grinded me down and I accepted that no matter how much I liked DPS, I had to role fill if we wanted to win games. So, after all these years I love getting my hands on a new support hero, but after four new supports this year (including Sombra's transition to the role), I'm more than satisfied with the role's current diversity of heroes.
But Team 4 is taking the criticism seriously, as Keller has addressed it directly. Aside from trying to convince players that shoehorning a hero into a role just because that was the plan 10 months ago isn't a great idea, he also explains how "game dev isn't always straightforward" and how the team needs "to adapt to create the best version of something".
I completely agree. I'd much rather have a hero that was crafted for a role holistically than one forced into it to fill a quota. Letting the people who know Overwatch the best, aka the devs, have the freedom to craft heroes and change them when needs be is what will ensure the best possible outcome.
This is such a non-issue, especially considering how strong the support roster currently is. Look at our poor tank players for example, forced to switch between Orisa and Mauga every game. Go give them some love and attention, lord knows they need the energy much more than us over in support.

title: Ashes of the Singularity 2 review: Some neat ideas undermined by a rubbish campaign and obtrusive generative AI
author: Rick Lane
text:
Need to know
What is it? RTS sequel in the lineage of Supreme Commander
Expect to pay: £32.50/$39
Developer: Oxide Games
Publisher: Stardock
Reviewed On: AMD Ryzen 5 3600, Nvidia 2080 Super, 32 GB RAM, Windows 10.
Multiplayer? Yes
Steam Deck? Unsupported
Link: Official site
Ashes of the Singularity 2 can't be faulted for scale. Much like its predecessor, the RTS sequel delivers on the promise of letting players control truly colossal armies. Rolling up huge globs of units and tossing them at your enemy lines in a giant, explosion-riddled mud fight is never subtle and only occasionally clever. But for any veteran RTS player, watching miles-long lines of armies clash is inevitably going to stir the soul.
Unfortunately, scale is also the sum of what Ashes of the Singularity 2 offers. As a sequel, it does little to build on the strengths of the original, while largely failing to address that first game's weaknesses. The campaign is terrible, the story borderline incomprehensible, and the whole experience is overshadowed by the spectre of generative AI.
Click rate
(Image credit: Stardock) Before we get into Ashes 2's numerous problems, I do want to give Oxide Games credit for one thing: for a game of this scale, Ashes of the Singularity 2 is remarkably easy to control. In terms of base-building, Ashes of the Singularity 2 is a largely familiar RTS affair. You build your production buildings, your resource harvesters, your defensive structures, and that's more or less it.
When it comes to unit recruitment, however, Ashes 2 is much more interesting. While units are still recruited individually, they're also automatically assigned into armies at the recruitment phase. You build a new army by queueing up all the units you want, and then when you're done, you assign a rally point for the army on the map, and all the units will just assemble there.
Once recruited, armies can be selected with the number keys and controlled like a single unit, and they tend to move and attack pretty intuitively, although pathfinding does struggle with narrow passes or rough terrain (which, to be fair are both things that real armies struggle with). This makes it very easy to oversee multiple armies at once.
(Image credit: Stardock) In addition, when in battle, you can replenish destroyed units at the press of a button, or simply set the army to reinforce automatically. It's another convenient touch, and encourages you to support your forces by constructing new production buildings close to the frontline.
It's not the only area where Ashes 2 displays an intuitive flourish. Alongside selecting the relevant structure from the menu, you can also construct harvester buildings directly from the resource node, while upgradeable buildings will often display an upgrade button over them that you can click. In terms of UI/UX design, Ashes 2 successfully minimises rooting through menus. Everything is accessible through shortcuts, directly on the screen, or a single menu layer.
This system does come at the cost of some finer control. Unit recruitment is bottlenecked to one unit per production building type, no matter how many buildings of that type you have. This means building an army composed of specific units (such as aerial units) takes longer, so armies tend to take a similar shape. On the subject of aerial units, they are a bit of a weak point for Ashes 2. Not only are they easily countered by AA units and emplacements, they also don't match the speed of ground units when in a mixed army, with a tendency to fly off and get themselves obliterated. Regardless, army control is by far the best thing about Ashes 2.
Mission slog
(Image credit: Stardock) The sequel does introduce some other new features, such as a new faction, the United Earth Forces; unfortunately it's the least interesting faction in the game.
The UEF is a deeply vanilla sci-fi army, composed of tanks, jets and human soldiers so tiny they get instantly lost once the match scales up. It's way less compelling than the many mechs of the Post-Human Coalition, or the robotic insects of the AI Substrate. Where the Substrate's dreadnought units include a giant squid that fires laser beams and a blimp that shoots swarms, the UEF gets a big tank and a knockoff Megazord. Granted, the tank functions as a mobile base. That's useful, but it isn't fun .
The UEF is also the sole focus of Ashes 2's campaign. This is disappointing, but it's also the least of the campaign's problems. It's composed of 10 missions, roughly half of which are rigid tutorials with passive AI that offers virtually no challenge whatsoever.
(Image credit: Stardock) The second half, which takes place in locations across the solar system, is better. The missions actually play with Ashes 2's scale and gradually let the AI off the leash. Indeed, the final two missions offer some pretty fierce resistance. But despite being set in locations like the Moon and on a weaponised asteroid bound for earth, they're also unambitious, meat and potatoes scenarios with no real twists or turns.
The result is four, maybe five hours of half-decent campaigning, which just isn't good enough in 2026.
The result is four, maybe five hours of half-decent campaigning, which just isn't good enough in 2026. It highlights how generous and meticulous Tempest Rising's campaigns were, built around thrilling, rapidly changing scenarios that sought to stretch the player's skills.
It doesn't help that the story is dreadful—a three way philosophy and ethics lecture between humans, AI, and uploaded post-human personality constructs. It's a parade of characters you never actually see babbling endlessly about the vague machinations of AI threats and whether or not post-humans are still the same people they were when they were bags of flesh and juice.
AI spy
(Image credit: Stardock) Ironically, the story is also where Oxide's use of generative AI is most evident. According to Ashes 2's Steam AI disclosure, Oxide used AI to "provide post processing effects and animation to art created by human Stardock artists for some of the campaign cutscenes" while "some cutscenes use Stardock human artist-made 3D assets with AI to composite the final shot." Finally, "some in-game unit barks, notifications, and a few minor characters use pre-generated ElevenLabs stock voices".
Frankly, I'm skeptical that this represents the limit of Oxide's AI use. All the character portraits look straight up AI generated to me, and the voice lines sound similarly infected. AI or not, it's something of a moot point because, either way, they're both awful. The portraits have that horrible, plasticky AI sheen to them, while the acting is often weirdly intoned in a way that does not help the narrative's bamboozling quality.
What bugs me most about Ashes 2's AI use, though, is that the RTS genre has such a rich heritage in cinematic storytelling. Warcraft 3, StarCraft 2 and Homeworld all successfully balanced their sci-fi grandeur with intimately human tales. Command & Conquer, meanwhile, was one of the earliest PC games to directly put a human face on videogame storytelling. From Kane to Tanya to Tim Curry escaping to the one place that hasn't been corrupted by capitalism, C&C's FMVs are often the thing that players most fondly remember.
(Image credit: Stardock) I understand that Oxide Games probably doesn't have a Tim Curry budget. But it also doesn't need it. C&C's FMVs aren't remembered because they're expensive, or even especially great storytelling. They're remembered because they're fun, silly, intensely human creations. You don't need a massive budget to replicate that. If Oxide Games stuck a beret on a programmer and had them ham it up in front of the camera, the result would be infinitely preferable to Ashes 2's airy, inhuman waffle.
With the campaign a write-off, you're left with multiplayer and skirmish mode. Skirmish is arguably where Ashes of the Singularity has always been at its strongest, and playing against the AI here is certainly better than the campaign, offering a wide range of difficulty levels that lets you find your own sweet-spot. Putting together a four-way grudge match, watching the scale of the conflict slowly build-out, commanding multiple armies on multiple fronts, you get a sense of what Ashes 2 could be.
None of the maps particularly spark joy.
Yet here too, there are problems. None of the maps particularly spark joy. It's a roster of generic biomes and moonscapes that offer little in the way of personality or artistic direction. Also—and this is a broader complaint—while I appreciate that Ashes 2 is meant to be a slow-burn affair, I think it is a little too slow overall. In particular, battles are too attrition-heavy, and beneath the visual fireworks, you don't necessarily feel the punch of your units in combat. When Dreadnought units clash, it should feel like two gods have descended from the heavens. Instead, it feels more like two giant snails squabbling over a particularly large leaf.
It's a shame, because the work Oxide has done to make such an unwieldy concept so, well, wieldy is impressive. Given more care and time (and less generative AI), I think this could have been a great RTS. But with the campaign such a bust, what you're paying for here is one new faction, a skirmish mode and multiplayer, and after 10 years, I just don't think that's sufficient for a sequel.

Also—and this is a broader complaint—while I appreciate that Ashes 2 is meant to be a slow-burn affair, I think it is a little too slow overall. In particular, battles are too attrition-heavy, and beneath the visual fireworks, you don't necessarily feel the punch of your units in combat. When Dreadnought units clash, it should feel like two gods have descended from the heavens. Instead, it feels more like two giant snails squabbling over a particularly large leaf.

It's a shame, because the work Oxide has done to make such an unwieldy concept so, well, wieldy is impressive. Given more care and time (and less generative AI), I think this could have been a great RTS. But with the campaign such a bust, what you're paying for here is one new faction, a skirmish mode and multiplayer, and after 10 years, I just don't think that's sufficient for a sequel.

title: World of Warcraft: Forever player turns their paladin into a near-unkillable healbot, solos a level 60 monster at level 30, and swims into the ocean
author: Harvey Randall
text:
World of Warcraft: Forever's having some teething issues with its new spellcaster itemisation. The idea, to sum it up quick, is that a lot of the power that was in spells innately has been pushed onto items, instead, with the intention to make it feel really good when you get a cool new staff as a mage, for instance.
This has had unintended consequences, as discovered by Rextroy (the same madlad who solos raid bosses ), as shared on YouTube . The problem is this: Gear in Forever can give a lot of raw power to your healing and damage spells, as part of the aforementioned changes. But that raw power also applies to lower-level healing spells, too.
In Forever (and in Classic), casting lower-level spells is a core part of managing your mana as a healer. In this instance, however, "the healing coefficient on healing power remains the same, which is around 43% [on a low level Flash of Light], so if I stack all healing green items, I get my healing power up towards 242," Rextroy explains.
This, combined with the Paladin talent Oath of Light (which slaps another 61 healing onto Flash of Light), along with Spiritual Focus and Concentration Aura, which makes it almost impossible for enemies to interrupt or push-back the casting of his Flash of Light, and this makes his paladin basically unkillable.
The low-rank version of his Flash of Light spell doesn't cost enough mana to outpace his natural mana regeneration, it heals for a bunch because of his gear, and enemies can't slow or interrupt it. Which makes him almost unkillable.
I say almost, because as his experimentations prove, he can still become stunned or crowd-controlled by high-level enemies. And there are limitations. While he can stand up to a level 60 enemy whacking on him, add two or three to the mix and he can no longer outpace their damage.
However, Rextroy finds a level 60 enemy he can kill, an abomination in Eastern Plaguelands, which he pulls using a bug that casts Echoes of Lordaeron, an anti-undead damage boost given to whichever faction controls the most towers in the zone, on enemies when he resurrects.
And sure, it takes 20 minutes. And sure, he can only kill it because the abomination has almost zero surprises, extra attacks, or abilities to stun him. But he still does it, getting a whopping… uh, 468 experience points for his trouble.
Perhaps the more game-breaking result of this build, then, is the fact that he can use it to out-pace fatigue damage, which generally stops players from swimming way out into the ocean. This lets him access a non-instanced version of the Drowned City dungeon, which is visible off the coast of Stranglethorn but cannot be visited outside of the dungeon without sleeping with the fishes.
While I think the extent of this build is probably something that'll get adjusted or patched out, I do sort of hope the spirit of it is kept the same—part of the promise of Forever was that weird item combinations or cool builds would emerge out of the woodwork and let folks do niche, but powerful things.
Perhaps it's not great that Rextroy can both tank and heal a dungeon with this setup at the same time, but I'd still like it to work in some capacity.

title: Final Fantasy 14 really wants Evercold to be the expansion everyone comes back to, so much so it's giving you 30 days free gametime if you've been gone long enough
author: Mollie Taylor
text:
Final Fantasy 14 is set to make some big changes when the upcoming expansion Evercold releases in February. An overhaul to combat, dailies, and new raid difficulties are set to shake things up and, hopefully, keep people sticking around for longer.
And judging by a recent Letter from the Producer , Naoki Yoshida really wants folks coming back to see what Evercold is all about. So much so that the game's offering 30 free days for long-gone adventurers… or a quick-and-dirty paid skip if you're so inclined.
"Encouraging players to return is no mean feat," Yoshida wrote. "People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons, including dissatisfaction and loss of interest. Although we continually update the game to address such issues, the fact remains that getting players to resume their journey is a difficult task indeed."
I can only assume that for that reason, the decision's been made to offer up a $9 cash shop item that'll skip you through Endwalker's patch story, as well as all of Dawntrail up until the final story patch. Now Final Fantasy 14 has offered paid story skips in the past—it still does—but this is the first time it's explicitly offered one for the current expansion. Usually the skips'll stop dead before the current expansion, meaning you still need to play through the newest story.
(Image credit: Square Enix) It's a pretty niche paid skip, too. You'll need to have at least completed Endwalker's main story and have a level 90 job on your chosen character, and even then you'll still have to level up to 100 in your own time in order to tackle the final patch quest of Dawntrail. But worry not, if you haven't played the game in six months, you'll be able to snap up 30 days of free game time until January 14. Plenty of time to get a job to max level and prepare for Evercold.
I'm mostly surprised by the introduction of this paid item because Yoshida has long been rather protective of the game's story. Something he admits in this very same letter: "I strongly believe that FF14 is a story-driven MMORPG," he wrote. "On top of that, skipping it all means you likely won't be familiar with the battle system and therefore will become a burden for other players in multiplayer content."
I do find it a little funny that Yoshida is worried that story skippers will weigh others down in dungeons and the like—I've played many a level 100 dungeon with folks who have clearly played enough to understand how to play yet still can't press their buttons properly.
But anyway, Yoshida does admit that there is a lot of story to get through. "The Hydaelyn and Zodiark saga alone encompasses five expansions' worth of content," he wrote. "And with Dawntrail marking the start of the second saga, plus the coming addition of Evercold, the story continues to unfold into something even larger."
It really does feel like Square Enix wants Evercold to mark a big resurgence for the game, one I really do hope pays off for the developer. I've been playing off-and-on since A Realm Reborn and have seen just about every evolution the game has taken, and also the ways it has stagnated over time. Its confidence in trying to draw people back has me excited for the changes that are coming.

title: 米哈游在二次元找了一年乐子，却找到了三次元的“入口”
text:
这次剧情真称得上是4.0开始到现在最爽的一集了。
11月11日，《崩坏：星穹铁道》4.7版本正式上线，从4.0一路铺陈至今的“幻月游戏”，终于以一场前所未有的神战大场面、一次完美收官的“开拓”，以及一声响彻寰宇的欢笑迎来了终幕，整个银河的命运也于此刻起真正休戚与共。
即便放在高手云集的年底，星铁新版本的“炸场”效果也相当亮眼：游戏不仅先后登顶中日韩App Store游戏畅销榜，故事的后劲也相当绵长，在玩家社区中掀起热议，直至现在仍有许多玩家乐此不疲地讨论着剧情的高光桥段。
但在热闹之外， 游戏日报 更在意着一个有意思的问题。正如二相乐园故事中始终贯穿的一个追问：片刻欢愉之后，究竟还能留下什么？而这一诘问，对于一款长线运营游戏而言也同样适用。 再精彩的剧情也终有曲终人散之时，当玩家收获的感动与满足逐渐褪去，又该如何让他们相信，下一段旅程依然值得同行？
在回顾整个“二相乐园”篇章后，我们忽然发现，米哈游似乎早已在为此准备答案了。过去近一年时间里，米哈游围绕“欢愉”，从游戏内到游戏外都找了不少乐子，这些看似各有侧重的尝试，实际上却在共同指向同一件事： 让故事所承载的情感不因落幕而消散，而积淀成下一场开拓之旅前进的薪柴。
一出好戏
对于以剧情为核心竞争力的二游而言，要让玩家愿意相信下一段旅程依然精彩，首先得让他们过去为故事投入的喜怒哀乐得到足够满意的回应，而在这一点上，星铁确实交出了一份颇有分量的答卷。 具体情节想必大家都已有所了解，这里就不再当文本或演出的复读机了，只聊聊最打动我们的几个地方。
首先，是故事自始至终对“欢愉”主题的高度统一。 从剧情之初，二相乐园便以荒诞跳脱、甚至有些无厘头的风格，让玩家直观领教了欢愉星神阿哈的不着调。但到了关乎宇宙命运的决战关口，这位乐子神总该严肃一点了吧？
事实却恰恰相反。谁能想到，肩负救世重任的主角团，竟然是驾驶着一艘蛋糕造型的“点星船”前去迎战贪饕的？而且说是点星船，但这完完全全就是“点心船”嘛——奶油、樱桃等甜点随处可见，可爱的幻造生物满地乱爬，整艘飞船的动力开关甚至是一座旋转木马，动力来源居然还是品尝美食后产生的“回味”。
更离谱的是，正式开战之前，阿哈还不忘再一次打破第四面墙，把玩家拉到由阿哈改造后的游戏登录界面。连公告、设置等寻常系统功能，都成了祂为玩家加油打气的一部分。
而这份看似有些不合时宜的欢脱，恰恰是整场决战最独特的魅力。拯救世界的故事并不少见，但在关乎宇宙存亡的危机面前，依然选择以一场盛大的狂欢回应绝望，才是独属于“欢愉”的浪漫。制作组没有为了抬高故事规格而牺牲叙事个性，反倒让高潮成为了故事主题上好的表达舞台。
其次，是过去伏笔的集中收束。 整个二相乐园篇章几乎一直在推翻玩家的既有认知，却很少让人觉得突兀，诸多悬念层层递进且彼此关联，又用接连不断的反转将玩家引向更深层的真相，每当谜底揭晓，都能带来一种“原来是这样”的恍然大悟感。
举个例子。早在4.4版本中 游戏日报 就纳闷过一件事：星穹列车都坠毁了这么久，拓星者的设计蓝图怎么还完好地留在列车里，又偏偏被年少的姬子捡到了？最终决战中也同样有件怪事：最终BOSS“疯狂”不过吃了主角团一套连招，怎么就从内部被引爆、炸成了一朵灿烂的笑脸烟花？
而这一切，竟都是阿哈早已布好的棋局。正是祂为姬子留下图纸，才埋下了星穹列车得以重返星海的可能性；祂也早早安排下归寂作为“谒者”参与幻月游戏的前提，使其在疯狂腹中接受庞大愿力而赢下游戏、成为新的欢愉星神，并最终因命途使命走向自我毁灭。直到最后，连作为对手的归寂，都不得不对这番布局心服口服。
这种叙事设计的妙处，不只是让悬念得到了解答，更在于让玩家以全新视角重新理解此前的故事。那些初看时莫名其妙的巧合，在真相揭晓后都有了新的意味。相比单纯依靠反转与新鲜感制造刺激，这些故事细节经由长期铺垫后的集中兑现，显然更值得反复品味。
与此同时，得到回应的不只有玩家对剧情的期待，还有过去对角色投入的感情。 我们不难发现，制作组在二相乐园篇的人物塑造上有一个鲜明倾向：让玩家早已熟悉的角色重新登台，直面过去的执念，补全各自的人生轨迹。无论是花火对“何为真我”的思考，还是刃与过往宿命及“倏忽”的彻底了断，他们都不是为成全主角而存在的附属品，而是拥有独立意志与追求的鲜活个体。
尤其是在故事尾声，阿哈微微欠身，以骑士之礼受封为开拓令使，更是让不少玩家为之动容的一笔，也是对“欢愉”与“开拓”关系最浪漫的诠释。欢愉给予漫长的开拓之旅更多值得回味的瞬间，开拓又让欢愉不再止于片刻的欢乐，而拥有奔赴下一场精彩的可能。两位星神跨越岁月的理解与情谊，又在新的开拓之旅中得到了延续。
随着未曾讲述的过往逐渐揭晓，旧友们并未随版本更迭而被遗忘，反而拥有了愈发完整的人生，玩家得以在一次次重逢中重新理解他们过去的言行，加深对角色的情感。这份持续得到回应的陪伴，既成就了4.7终局群像剧的魅力，也让玩家有了继续陪伴他们走下去的理由。
而这一切，又回到了二相乐园始终在探讨的一个问题：当欢愉注定消逝，人们是否还有必要继续追求欢愉？对此，制作组借由阿哈的故事给出了一个答案——欢愉的意义从不在于永恒，而在于那些曾经真切经历过的每一个瞬间，即便故事终将落幕，那些经历也不会因此失去意义。正因为片刻欢愉能够留下长久的回响，引发对未来的期待，人们才有理由在告别一段旅程后，依然满心雀跃地奔赴下一场相遇。
这也让我们得以窥见星铁“开拓”主题所拥有的广阔叙事空间。开拓的魅力，正在于它不预设旅途的终点，也不要求同行者拥有完全相同的信念，而是在探索未知的过程中，让不同命途得以相遇、碰撞，甚至赋予彼此新的意义，今日是欢愉，未来又会和其他命途擦出怎样精彩的火花？光是想想便足够令人期待。
当玩家过去的投入都能在旅程中得到新的回应，那些曾经打动自己的故事与人物，依然拥有值得期待的明天，自然便有了继续同行的理由。 而这份信任，正是星铁告别二相乐园、驶向下一站时最为珍贵的收获。
“第四面墙”，也拦不下欢愉
而这份同行信任的积淀，显然并不止源于游戏内的故事。 过去一年里，米哈游还在尝试让玩家与游戏之间的情感联系走进现实，让那些曾经在故事中感受到的美好，拥有更加具体的落点。
最直观的体现，便是日益丰富的线下活动。 今年五一期间，米哈游将剧情中二相乐园的“星铁FES”搬到了上海，举办了为期三天的2026星铁LAND嘉年华。从二相乐园的霓虹灯影，再到由玩家共同参与的文化集市，那些令人印象深刻的场景纷纷走入了现实。而在此之前，围绕东方明珠塔展开的“幻月新游戏”特别企划，更将游戏中的阵营争夺与愿力比拼带进了三次元，让现实也成为了欢愉游戏的舞台。
星铁LAND场照
当虚拟世界中的节庆成为现实里的聚会，素未谋面的开拓者们因共同的热爱而相聚，玩家便不再只是故事的观众，更成为了这场狂欢的亲历者与创造者。那些曾经只存在于屏幕中的共同记忆，化作了现实中真实的相遇，让这份情感有了更具体的延续。
不过，相比让玩家亲身体验故事里的欢愉，米哈游所做的另一件事，或许更能体现其对“欢愉”与“开拓”的理解——那便是“齐乐绒绒大冒险”系列公益行动， 也是在玩家调侃中，星铁荣获GamingonPhone Awards (GPA)“最佳社区奖”的原因之一。
玩笑归玩笑，但这场系列公益行动确实值得我们认真聊聊。在首期活动“星穹下的格桑花”中，星铁向公益救助项目捐赠100万元，为中西部地区患有先天性疾病的儿童提供医疗救治等帮助。到了第二期“当一颗星照亮夜空”，项目组又将目光投向了乡村教育，在星铁的帮助下，孩子们走出大山，来到酒泉卫星发射中心，亲眼见证了神舟二十三号载人飞船发射升空。亲历了一场过去只能在课本与电视中仰望的航天梦想。
而在最新一期“抵达彩色的彼方”活动中，与此前不同，星铁又将目光投向了一种不那么容易被看见的困境——心理健康。项目组向北京尚善公益基金会捐赠100万元，并联合全国10余家民间抗郁组织，为有需要的人提供心理健康支持与陪伴。
同期发布的公益短片中，一名少年因不被理解的疲惫与情绪，化作了黑白世界里一只蜷缩的小刺猬，但在列车组的小动物伙伴们到来后，灰暗的世界终于逐渐活泛了起来。制作组还邀请玩家为失去颜色的画作重新上色，让玩家们不再只是隔着屏幕观看他人的故事，也能亲自为这份关怀添上一笔，将对心理健康议题的关注转化为一场可以共同参与的行动。
这些公益活动自然无法解决现实中的所有难题，但让更多人愿意认真倾听并理解他人的处境，本身就是改变的开始。而回望这三期公益，我们也会发现，它们其实也在以另一种方式回应二相乐园对“欢愉”的探讨：欢愉从来没有统一的标准，每个人都应当有机会找到属于自己的快乐，追求自己的幸福。
如果说“欢愉”关乎对幸福的不同向往，那“开拓”便是让这些向往不止于向往。开拓的动人之处，从来不只是因为仰望星空的浪漫，更在于面对现实阻碍时，开拓从未放弃迈出改变的第一步以上三期公益活动，都在尝试打破不同的现实局限，让更多人拥有追求欢愉、追求幸福的可能。于是，“欢愉”与“开拓”便在这些行动中有了具体的交汇：既珍视每个人不同的愿望，也愿意为这些愿望的实现而付诸行动。
这也正是游戏日报最关注的地方。 过去谈论游戏的叙事价值，我们大多关注它如何通过故事传递打动玩家的理念，但星铁正在尝试走得更远，让故事所表达的价值，能在现实中产生切实的回响。 当“欢愉”与“开拓”不再只是故事中的口号，而成为现实中照亮他人的点点星火，那些曾经打动玩家的情感与理想，也便有机会沉淀为更长久的价值认同。而这，又何尝不是同行信任的另一种积累？
下一站的方向
当然，无论是精彩的故事，还是游戏内外不断延伸的情感联系，要真正建立与玩家的长期信任，终究绕不开一个现实基础： 游戏本身凭什么让玩家相信，下一段旅程依然值得期待？
随着运营时间拉长，一些问题在所难免地浮现而出：新角色不断登场，老角色该何去何从？玩法机制持续创新，又该如何避免数值膨胀？当游戏内容越来越丰富，玩家又是否有足够的时间与精力跟上更新？问题看似五花八门，实则都关乎着同一件事：玩家过去的投入，能否在未来继续得到尊重与回报？
近期，《崩坏：星穹铁道》在韩国首尔举行的HoYoverse媒体巡回活动中接受采访时，首席设计师安承男便对这些问题做出了回应。
首先是新老角色的价值平衡 。4.7版本推出的“奇缘星魂”便是制作组的一次尝试，通过全新的战斗机制与专属演出，让老角色重新焕发活力。未来，制作组也将结合剧情、玩法等不同维度，探索适合各个角色的呈现方式，让玩家曾经喜爱的角色持续展现新的魅力。
其次是玩法创新与数值膨胀之间的平衡。 作为一款回合制RPG，星铁拥有扩展性较强的基础框架，也因此不断尝试新的命途机制。但正如安承男所言，制作组并不希望玩家只能依赖当年推出的新命途角色，而希望加强新旧角色之间的搭配可能。换句话说，新机制的加入，理应为玩家创造出更多选择，而非让过去的积累失去价值。
最后，则是内容扩张与玩家体验负担之间的平衡。 随着游戏体量不断增长，丰富的内容也可能带来更高的理解门槛与追赶成本。因此，制作组正在优化养成流程、降低新玩法的入门门槛，推出如“货币战争”这类让玩家既能轻松上手，又值得深入钻研的玩法内容。
将这些尝试放在一起便能发现，米哈游正在着手解决的，其实是长线二游稳定运营所需要解决的一道核心命题： 如何让持续增长的新内容，成为玩家过去积累的延伸，而非让版本更新成为对既有投入的重新洗牌?
只有相信过去的心血不会被轻易辜负，玩家才有信心继续为游戏的未来投入时间与感情，而更稳定的角色价值、玩法生态与体验节奏，为玩家建立长期体验预期，正是星铁制作组现在正在做的事情，为这份信心提供切实依据。这份逐渐累积的信任，也将让星铁在一次次内容高潮之后，拥有支撑玩家长期同行的根本动力，走出更持续的长线运营。
而在日常运营层面，米哈游也在通过更加直接的方式回应玩家。 比如4.7版本不仅提供了新一批限定五星角色自选，还准备了奇缘星魂、星轨专票等多项福利，并包装成“阿哈赠礼”的形式融入版本氛围，让福利回馈也成为这场欢愉盛宴的一部分。
这些举措自然无法一次性解决长线运营的所有难题，但至少表明，制作组不仅在规划未来的开拓方向，也在努力回应玩家当下的实际需求，毕竟，长期信任的建立，既需要对未来的明确规划，也离不开一次次切实可感的体会。星铁已经为此迈出了新的一步，至于成效如何，仍有待后续版本检验。
至此，二相乐园的篇章终于告一段落。欢愉虽终有散场的一刻，但那些共同经历的故事、积累的情感，以及由此建立的信任，却不会随之轻易消散，反而会在未来的开拓中不断焕发新的生命力。而一场欢愉好戏最好的结局，也从来不是让观众久久不愿离席，而是当列车再次鸣笛启程时，我们依然愿意怀着对未知的期待奔赴下一场相遇，为新的故事抚掌驻足。

这次剧情真称得上是4.0开始到现在最爽的一集了。


11月11日，《崩坏：星穹铁道》4.7版本正式上线，从4.0一路铺陈至今的“幻月游戏”，终于以一场前所未有的神战大场面、一次完美收官的“开拓”，以及一声响彻寰宇的欢笑迎来了终幕，整个银河的命运也于此刻起真正休戚与共。


即便放在高手云集的年底，星铁新版本的“炸场”效果也相当亮眼：游戏不仅先后登顶中日韩App Store游戏畅销榜，故事的后劲也相当绵长，在玩家社区中掀起热议，直至现在仍有许多玩家乐此不疲地讨论着剧情的高光桥段。



但在热闹之外，游戏日报更在意着一个有意思的问题。正如二相乐园故事中始终贯穿的一个追问：片刻欢愉之后，究竟还能留下什么？而这一诘问，对于一款长线运营游戏而言也同样适用。再精彩的剧情也终有曲终人散之时，当玩家收获的感动与满足逐渐褪去，又该如何让他们相信，下一段旅程依然值得同行？


在回顾整个“二相乐园”篇章后，我们忽然发现，米哈游似乎早已在为此准备答案了。过去近一年时间里，米哈游围绕“欢愉”，从游戏内到游戏外都找了不少乐子，这些看似各有侧重的尝试，实际上却在共同指向同一件事：让故事所承载的情感不因落幕而消散，而积淀成下一场开拓之旅前进的薪柴。


一出好戏


对于以剧情为核心竞争力的二游而言，要让玩家愿意相信下一段旅程依然精彩，首先得让他们过去为故事投入的喜怒哀乐得到足够满意的回应，而在这一点上，星铁确实交出了一份颇有分量的答卷。具体情节想必大家都已有所了解，这里就不再当文本或演出的复读机了，只聊聊最打动我们的几个地方。


首先，是故事自始至终对“欢愉”主题的高度统一。从剧情之初，二相乐园便以荒诞跳脱、甚至有些无厘头的风格，让玩家直观领教了欢愉星神阿哈的不着调。但到了关乎宇宙命运的决战关口，这位乐子神总该严肃一点了吧？


事实却恰恰相反。谁能想到，肩负救世重任的主角团，竟然是驾驶着一艘蛋糕造型的“点星船”前去迎战贪饕的？而且说是点星船，但这完完全全就是“点心船”嘛——奶油、樱桃等甜点随处可见，可爱的幻造生物满地乱爬，整艘飞船的动力开关甚至是一座旋转木马，动力来源居然还是品尝美食后产生的“回味”。



更离谱的是，正式开战之前，阿哈还不忘再一次打破第四面墙，把玩家拉到由阿哈改造后的游戏登录界面。连公告、设置等寻常系统功能，都成了祂为玩家加油打气的一部分。



而这份看似有些不合时宜的欢脱，恰恰是整场决战最独特的魅力。拯救世界的故事并不少见，但在关乎宇宙存亡的危机面前，依然选择以一场盛大的狂欢回应绝望，才是独属于“欢愉”的浪漫。制作组没有为了抬高故事规格而牺牲叙事个性，反倒让高潮成为了故事主题上好的表达舞台。


其次，是过去伏笔的集中收束。整个二相乐园篇章几乎一直在推翻玩家的既有认知，却很少让人觉得突兀，诸多悬念层层递进且彼此关联，又用接连不断的反转将玩家引向更深层的真相，每当谜底揭晓，都能带来一种“原来是这样”的恍然大悟感。


举个例子。早在4.4版本中游戏日报就纳闷过一件事：星穹列车都坠毁了这么久，拓星者的设计蓝图怎么还完好地留在列车里，又偏偏被年少的姬子捡到了？最终决战中也同样有件怪事：最终BOSS“疯狂”不过吃了主角团一套连招，怎么就从内部被引爆、炸成了一朵灿烂的笑脸烟花？



而这一切，竟都是阿哈早已布好的棋局。正是祂为姬子留下图纸，才埋下了星穹列车得以重返星海的可能性；祂也早早安排下归寂作为“谒者”参与幻月游戏的前提，使其在疯狂腹中接受庞大愿力而赢下游戏、成为新的欢愉星神，并最终因命途使命走向自我毁灭。直到最后，连作为对手的归寂，都不得不对这番布局心服口服。



这种叙事设计的妙处，不只是让悬念得到了解答，更在于让玩家以全新视角重新理解此前的故事。那些初看时莫名其妙的巧合，在真相揭晓后都有了新的意味。相比单纯依靠反转与新鲜感制造刺激，这些故事细节经由长期铺垫后的集中兑现，显然更值得反复品味。


与此同时，得到回应的不只有玩家对剧情的期待，还有过去对角色投入的感情。我们不难发现，制作组在二相乐园篇的人物塑造上有一个鲜明倾向：让玩家早已熟悉的角色重新登台，直面过去的执念，补全各自的人生轨迹。无论是花火对“何为真我”的思考，还是刃与过往宿命及“倏忽”的彻底了断，他们都不是为成全主角而存在的附属品，而是拥有独立意志与追求的鲜活个体。



尤其是在故事尾声，阿哈微微欠身，以骑士之礼受封为开拓令使，更是让不少玩家为之动容的一笔，也是对“欢愉”与“开拓”关系最浪漫的诠释。欢愉给予漫长的开拓之旅更多值得回味的瞬间，开拓又让欢愉不再止于片刻的欢乐，而拥有奔赴下一场精彩的可能。两位星神跨越岁月的理解与情谊，又在新的开拓之旅中得到了延续。



随着未曾讲述的过往逐渐揭晓，旧友们并未随版本更迭而被遗忘，反而拥有了愈发完整的人生，玩家得以在一次次重逢中重新理解他们过去的言行，加深对角色的情感。这份持续得到回应的陪伴，既成就了4.7终局群像剧的魅力，也让玩家有了继续陪伴他们走下去的理由。



而这一切，又回到了二相乐园始终在探讨的一个问题：当欢愉注定消逝，人们是否还有必要继续追求欢愉？对此，制作组借由阿哈的故事给出了一个答案——欢愉的意义从不在于永恒，而在于那些曾经真切经历过的每一个瞬间，即便故事终将落幕，那些经历也不会因此失去意义。正因为片刻欢愉能够留下长久的回响，引发对未来的期待，人们才有理由在告别一段旅程后，依然满心雀跃地奔赴下一场相遇。



这也让我们得以窥见星铁“开拓”主题所拥有的广阔叙事空间。开拓的魅力，正在于它不预设旅途的终点，也不要求同行者拥有完全相同的信念，而是在探索未知的过程中，让不同命途得以相遇、碰撞，甚至赋予彼此新的意义，今日是欢愉，未来又会和其他命途擦出怎样精彩的火花？光是想想便足够令人期待。


当玩家过去的投入都能在旅程中得到新的回应，那些曾经打动自己的故事与人物，依然拥有值得期待的明天，自然便有了继续同行的理由。而这份信任，正是星铁告别二相乐园、驶向下一站时最为珍贵的收获。


“第四面墙”，也拦不下欢愉


而这份同行信任的积淀，显然并不止源于游戏内的故事。过去一年里，米哈游还在尝试让玩家与游戏之间的情感联系走进现实，让那些曾经在故事中感受到的美好，拥有更加具体的落点。


最直观的体现，便是日益丰富的线下活动。今年五一期间，米哈游将剧情中二相乐园的“星铁FES”搬到了上海，举办了为期三天的2026星铁LAND嘉年华。从二相乐园的霓虹灯影，再到由玩家共同参与的文化集市，那些令人印象深刻的场景纷纷走入了现实。而在此之前，围绕东方明珠塔展开的“幻月新游戏”特别企划，更将游戏中的阵营争夺与愿力比拼带进了三次元，让现实也成为了欢愉游戏的舞台。


星铁LAND场照


当虚拟世界中的节庆成为现实里的聚会，素未谋面的开拓者们因共同的热爱而相聚，玩家便不再只是故事的观众，更成为了这场狂欢的亲历者与创造者。那些曾经只存在于屏幕中的共同记忆，化作了现实中真实的相遇，让这份情感有了更具体的延续。


不过，相比让玩家亲身体验故事里的欢愉，米哈游所做的另一件事，或许更能体现其对“欢愉”与“开拓”的理解——那便是“齐乐绒绒大冒险”系列公益行动，也是在玩家调侃中，星铁荣获GamingonPhone Awards (GPA)“最佳社区奖”的原因之一。


玩笑归玩笑，但这场系列公益行动确实值得我们认真聊聊。在首期活动“星穹下的格桑花”中，星铁向公益救助项目捐赠100万元，为中西部地区患有先天性疾病的儿童提供医疗救治等帮助。到了第二期“当一颗星照亮夜空”，项目组又将目光投向了乡村教育，在星铁的帮助下，孩子们走出大山，来到酒泉卫星发射中心，亲眼见证了神舟二十三号载人飞船发射升空。亲历了一场过去只能在课本与电视中仰望的航天梦想。



而在最新一期“抵达彩色的彼方”活动中，与此前不同，星铁又将目光投向了一种不那么容易被看见的困境——心理健康。项目组向北京尚善公益基金会捐赠100万元，并联合全国10余家民间抗郁组织，为有需要的人提供心理健康支持与陪伴。


同期发布的公益短片中，一名少年因不被理解的疲惫与情绪，化作了黑白世界里一只蜷缩的小刺猬，但在列车组的小动物伙伴们到来后，灰暗的世界终于逐渐活泛了起来。制作组还邀请玩家为失去颜色的画作重新上色，让玩家们不再只是隔着屏幕观看他人的故事，也能亲自为这份关怀添上一笔，将对心理健康议题的关注转化为一场可以共同参与的行动。



这些公益活动自然无法解决现实中的所有难题，但让更多人愿意认真倾听并理解他人的处境，本身就是改变的开始。而回望这三期公益，我们也会发现，它们其实也在以另一种方式回应二相乐园对“欢愉”的探讨：欢愉从来没有统一的标准，每个人都应当有机会找到属于自己的快乐，追求自己的幸福。


如果说“欢愉”关乎对幸福的不同向往，那“开拓”便是让这些向往不止于向往。开拓的动人之处，从来不只是因为仰望星空的浪漫，更在于面对现实阻碍时，开拓从未放弃迈出改变的第一步以上三期公益活动，都在尝试打破不同的现实局限，让更多人拥有追求欢愉、追求幸福的可能。于是，“欢愉”与“开拓”便在这些行动中有了具体的交汇：既珍视每个人不同的愿望，也愿意为这些愿望的实现而付诸行动。



这也正是游戏日报最关注的地方。过去谈论游戏的叙事价值，我们大多关注它如何通过故事传递打动玩家的理念，但星铁正在尝试走得更远，让故事所表达的价值，能在现实中产生切实的回响。当“欢愉”与“开拓”不再只是故事中的口号，而成为现实中照亮他人的点点星火，那些曾经打动玩家的情感与理想，也便有机会沉淀为更长久的价值认同。而这，又何尝不是同行信任的另一种积累？


下一站的方向


当然，无论是精彩的故事，还是游戏内外不断延伸的情感联系，要真正建立与玩家的长期信任，终究绕不开一个现实基础：游戏本身凭什么让玩家相信，下一段旅程依然值得期待？


随着运营时间拉长，一些问题在所难免地浮现而出：新角色不断登场，老角色该何去何从？玩法机制持续创新，又该如何避免数值膨胀？当游戏内容越来越丰富，玩家又是否有足够的时间与精力跟上更新？问题看似五花八门，实则都关乎着同一件事：玩家过去的投入，能否在未来继续得到尊重与回报？


近期，《崩坏：星穹铁道》在韩国首尔举行的HoYoverse媒体巡回活动中接受采访时，首席设计师安承男便对这些问题做出了回应。



首先是新老角色的价值平衡。4.7版本推出的“奇缘星魂”便是制作组的一次尝试，通过全新的战斗机制与专属演出，让老角色重新焕发活力。未来，制作组也将结合剧情、玩法等不同维度，探索适合各个角色的呈现方式，让玩家曾经喜爱的角色持续展现新的魅力。


其次是玩法创新与数值膨胀之间的平衡。作为一款回合制RPG，星铁拥有扩展性较强的基础框架，也因此不断尝试新的命途机制。但正如安承男所言，制作组并不希望玩家只能依赖当年推出的新命途角色，而希望加强新旧角色之间的搭配可能。换句话说，新机制的加入，理应为玩家创造出更多选择，而非让过去的积累失去价值。


最后，则是内容扩张与玩家体验负担之间的平衡。随着游戏体量不断增长，丰富的内容也可能带来更高的理解门槛与追赶成本。因此，制作组正在优化养成流程、降低新玩法的入门门槛，推出如“货币战争”这类让玩家既能轻松上手，又值得深入钻研的玩法内容。


将这些尝试放在一起便能发现，米哈游正在着手解决的，其实是长线二游稳定运营所需要解决的一道核心命题：如何让持续增长的新内容，成为玩家过去积累的延伸，而非让版本更新成为对既有投入的重新洗牌?


只有相信过去的心血不会被轻易辜负，玩家才有信心继续为游戏的未来投入时间与感情，而更稳定的角色价值、玩法生态与体验节奏，为玩家建立长期体验预期，正是星铁制作组现在正在做的事情，为这份信心提供切实依据。这份逐渐累积的信任，也将让星铁在一次次内容高潮之后，拥有支撑玩家长期同行的根本动力，走出更持续的长线运营。


而在日常运营层面，米哈游也在通过更加直接的方式回应玩家。比如4.7版本不仅提供了新一批限定五星角色自选，还准备了奇缘星魂、星轨专票等多项福利，并包装成“阿哈赠礼”的形式融入版本氛围，让福利回馈也成为这场欢愉盛宴的一部分。



这些举措自然无法一次性解决长线运营的所有难题，但至少表明，制作组不仅在规划未来的开拓方向，也在努力回应玩家当下的实际需求，毕竟，长期信任的建立，既需要对未来的明确规划，也离不开一次次切实可感的体会。星铁已经为此迈出了新的一步，至于成效如何，仍有待后续版本检验。


至此，二相乐园的篇章终于告一段落。欢愉虽终有散场的一刻，但那些共同经历的故事、积累的情感，以及由此建立的信任，却不会随之轻易消散，反而会在未来的开拓中不断焕发新的生命力。而一场欢愉好戏最好的结局，也从来不是让观众久久不愿离席，而是当列车再次鸣笛启程时，我们依然愿意怀着对未知的期待奔赴下一场相遇，为新的故事抚掌驻足。

title: 存量时代的手游增长新法则：如何从“抢流量”走向“读懂玩家”？
text:
10月28日下午，Unity U:LIVE 首期线上直播圆满落幕。在持续两个多小时的分享中，Unity 广告业务中国区高级商务经理 Kenny Jing、Unity 广告业务中国区客户经理 Vesper Chang 与 Sensor Tower 游戏行业销售总监 Xiang Tian 齐聚线上。
面对大盘承压与大环境变化，三位嘉宾从市场趋势、智能投放与深度变现等角度展开拆解。尽管讨论视角各异，但指向了同一个行业核心议题：在新增玩家日益稀缺的存量时代，如何更早辨识并留住真正具备高价值的用户？
下载大国不再等同于增长市场
Sensor Tower 游戏行业销售总监 Xiang Tian 指出，2026 年上半年，手游市场呈现出下载量收缩、内购收入小幅回落、每次下载内购收入上升的趋势。同期，手游下载量为 226 亿次，同比下降 11.8%；内购收入为 277 亿美元，同比下降 2.0%；总使用时长同比增长 0.3%。每次下载内购收入（RPD）达到 1.23 美元，同比增长 11.0%。市场表现的分化，让区域、品类与变现模式的选择变得更加重要。
数据表明：“玩家并未离开游戏，只是新玩家流入放缓。”市场增量呈现出三大结构性特征：
● 不同区域市场的增长节奏正在分化：印度、巴西、印尼等主要下载市场的下载量出现下滑。收入方面，土耳其同比增长 18.9%，意大利、英国、澳大利亚、法国也实现正增长；美国、日本、韩国合计收入同比下滑超过 8%。出海团队需采取“小规模测试-按表现调投”策略。
● 品类结构分化：益智解谜与混合休闲品类内购收入大幅增长，呈现“收入增长与下载收缩并存”的特点。
● 评估逻辑转向：渠道组合并无通用模板，不同品类与变现模式，对高价值用户的衡量重点有所不同。团队在扩量时需综合目标回收周期内的用户累计净收入与获客成本（CPI），并结合广告支出回报率（ROAS）、预计用户生命周期价值（LTV）和回收周期，判断是否扩大投放。
买量转型：从“买点击”走向“买价值”
“过去拼出价、拼流量的粗放买量，把用户看作可替换的点击，结果必然是成本越来越高，LTV 天花板越来越低。”Unity 广告业务中国区高级商务经理 Kenny Jing 表示。
针对这一困局，Unity 带来了背后的深度解法——Vector 模型。作为 Unity Ads 驱动核心，Vector 可整合开发、购买、运行、玩家属性、游戏内表现、竞价及归因等七层数据。目前全球 Top 1000 手游中 70% 基于 Unity 引擎开发，月触达活跃设备达 30 亿台。2026 年一季度数据显示，Unity Ads 投放规模同比增长 95%，美区 D7 广告 ARPU 上涨 78%，D28 内购 ARPU 上涨 68%。
针对具体的投放操作，他拆解了出价机制：出价 = 预测收入 / ROAS 目标。目标设定过高会导致出价与 eCPM 偏低，进而失去竞价优势；而对于跑不出量的项目，“正确的做法是下调 ROAS 预期，而非盲目上调。”若预算花不满，建议每3至5天下调 10% 目标；同时在上线前，确保 MMP 回传窗口设定不低于 180 天。
运营盘活：激活被忽略的 98% 非付费人群
除了前端获取，后端的深度运营同样决定增长上限。Unity 广告业务中国区客户经理 Vesper Chang 分享了一组行业常态数据：手游行业中约 98% 的用户不会在游戏内直接付费。如何留住这部分用户并实现商业化转化？答案在于“用时间换资源”的机制创新。
Offerwall（积分墙） 允许玩家通过完成其他应用内的指定任务，换取当前游戏的虚拟货币。Unity 统计显示，美国市场积分墙在 iOS 端的 eCPM 约为激励视频的 8 倍，安卓端约为 6 倍；完成过任务的用户，其后续留存率提升 3 至 4 倍。
Vesper 补充道，运营积分墙的关键在于双向联动，变现靠“前置入口+节日促销”提效率，买量靠“CPE+tROAS”攻质量。
变现优化策略：
1. 显眼入口：将入口尽可能前置并放在第一屏；
2. 节点促销与通知：在节假日开启虚拟货币促销，并搭配 M2E（Message-to-Earn）弹窗与横幅通知。例如，游戏《Rival Stars Horse Racing》在劳动节叠加 M2E 通知后，积分墙广告收入实现了近乎翻倍的增长。
买量优化策略：
1. 丰富获客渠道：将 Offerwall 升级为获客渠道，广告主可根据产品类型、点位设置情况选择合适的 Offer 类型，并以 CPE 结算模式为用户完成任务付费，获取高价值用户。
2. tROAS 驱动买量：每日奖励任务可开启 tROAS，算法依托 IAP/IAA/Hybrid 收入模型进行动态阶梯出价，基于D3/D7收益筛选高价值用户，提升投放效率。
Playrix 旗下的《Township》在美国 iOS 的投放规模扩大至 4.5 倍且 ROAS 持续达标；Vizor 旗下的《Klondike Adventures》在三个月内将美国安卓端的投放规模提升了 380%。
存量时代的手游增长新法则
回顾整场直播，从 Sensor Tower 对大盘趋势与高留存模式的剖析，到 Unity Vector 解决“精确买到谁”、再到 Offerwall 解决“剩下 98% 非付费用户的长线运营”，三位嘉宾给出的方案逻辑环环相扣。
这也揭示了存量时代下手游出海与本土增长的真正法则：增量竞争的本质是效率竞争，手游商业化必须从“粗放式抢夺流量”转向“深度读懂玩家”。唯有将预算与资源精准投向会长期留存、产生深层价值的用户，才能在存量市场中建立起抗周期、高回报的长期增长曲线。
关于 Unity
Unity (纽约证券交易所:U) 是全球领先的创作者工具平台，赋能创作者进行实时游戏、广应用和体验的跨平台开发和增长，支持平台包括手机、PC、游戏主机和空间计算。
